[ Herb Kay Undergraduate Lecture, University of California, Santa Barbara Economics Department ]

Ch. 4 // Talk Nine // Academic Economics: Strengths and Faults after Considering Interdisciplinary Needs
Herb Kay Undergraduate Lecture, University of California, Santa Barbara Economics Department

Academic Economics: Strengths and Faults after Considering Interdisciplinary Needs学术经济学的长处与缺陷

I have outlined some remarks in a rough way, and after I’m finished talking from that outline, I’ll take questions as long as anybody can endure listening, until they drag me away to wherever else I’m supposed to go.

我已经大致列好了一些发言要点，等我照着提纲讲完之后，只要你们还能忍受听下去，我就会一直回答提问，直到有人把我拖去我该去的下一个地方为止。

As you might guess, I agreed to do this because the subject of getting the soft sciences so they talk better to each other has been one that has interested me for decades. And, of course, economics is, in many respects, the queen of the soft sciences. It’s expected to be better than the rest. It’s my view that economics is better at the multidisciplinary stuff than the rest of soft science. It’s also my view that it’s still lousy, and I’d like to discuss this failure in this talk.

你们大概能猜到，我之所以答应来做这次演讲，是因为“如何让各门软科学更好地相互对话”这个主题让我感兴趣了几十年。当然，从很多方面来说，经济学都是软科学中的皇后。人们期望它比其他软科学做得更好。我认为，比起其他软科学，经济学在多学科研究上做得更好。但我也认为它依然很糟糕，而我想在这次演讲中谈谈这种失败。

我认为，比起其他软科学，经济学在多学科研究上做得更好。但我也认为它依然很糟糕。

“It’s my view that economics is better at the multidisciplinary stuff than the rest of soft science. It’s also my view that it’s still lousy.”323Black belt in chutzpah厚脸皮黑带（厚颜高手）我的看法是：比起其他软科学，经济学在跨学科这件事上做得更好；我也同样认为，它依然糟得很。（这话说得厚颜无耻，堪称黑带级）

As I talk about strengths and weaknesses in academic economics, one interesting fact you are entitled to know is that I never took a course in economics. And with this striking lack of credentials, you may wonder why I have the chutzpah to be up here giving this talk. The answer is I have a black belt in chutzpah. I was born with it. Some people, like some of the women I know, have a black belt in spending. They were born with that. But what they gave me was a black belt in chutzpah.

在我谈论学院派经济学322Academic economics学院派经济学的长处与短处时，你们有权知道一件有趣的事：我从未修过一门经济学课程。既然我毫无资历可言，你们或许会奇怪，我哪来的厚脸皮站在这里发表演讲。答案是：我的厚脸皮是黑带水平。这是天生的。有些人——比如我认识的某些女性——在花钱方面是黑带水平，她们天生如此。但赋予我的，却是厚脸皮的黑带。

I come from two peculiar strands of experience that may have given me some useful economic insights. One is Berkshire Hathaway, and the other is my personal educational history. Berkshire, of course, has finally gotten interesting. When Warren took over Berkshire, the market capitalization was about $10 million. Forty-something years later, there are not many more shares outstanding now than there were then, and the market capitalization is about $100 billion, $10,000 for one. And since that has happened, year after year, in kind of a grind-ahead fashion with very few failures, it eventually drew some attention, indicating that maybe Warren and I knew something useful in microeconomics.

我有两种特殊的经历，或许给了我一些有用的经济洞察。一是伯克希尔·哈撒韦（Berkshire Hathaway），二是我个人的教育经历。当然，伯克希尔终于变得有意思了。沃伦·巴菲特（Warren Buffett）接管伯克希尔时，市值约为1000万美元。四十多年后，流通股数量比那时并没有多多少，而市值约为1000亿美元，每股1万美元。这种情况年复一年地发生，以一种稳步推进、鲜有失败的方式，最终引起了注意，说明或许沃伦和我在微观经济学上懂得一些有用的东西。

For a long time, there was a Nobel Prize–winning economist who explained Berkshire Hathaway’s success as follows:

有很长一段时间，一位获得诺贝尔奖的经济学家是这样解释伯克希尔·哈撒韦的成功的：

First, he said Berkshire beat the market in common stock investing through one sigma of luck because nobody could beat the market except by luck. This hard-form version of efficient-market theory was taught in most schools of economics at the time. People were taught that nobody could beat the market. Next, the professor went to two sigmas, and three sigmas, and four sigmas, and when he finally got to six sigmas of luck, people were laughing so hard he stopped doing it.

首先，他说伯克希尔能在普通股投资上战胜市场，靠的是一个运气西格玛，因为除了运气，没有人能战胜市场。这种僵化的有效市场理论，当时在大多数经济学院里都被当作教条讲授。人们被教导说，没有人能战胜市场。接着，这位教授又加到两个西格玛、三个西格玛、四个西格玛，等他终于说到六个运气西格玛时，人们笑得前仰后合，他也就不再往下说了。

Then, he reversed the explanation 180 degrees. He said, “No, it was still six sigmas, but it was six sigmas of skill.” Well, this very sad history demonstrates the truth of Benjamin Franklin’s324Benjamin Franklin本杰明·富兰克林 observation in Poor Richard’s Almanack:325 “If you would persuade, appeal to interest and not to reason.” The man changed his silly view when his incentives made him change it and notxa0before.

如果你要说服别人，诉诸利益，而非诉诸理性。

“If you would persuade, appeal to interest and nottoxa0reason.”若你想说服别人，要诉诸利益，而非诉诸理性。

I watched the same thing happen at the Jules Stein Eye Institute at UCLA. I asked at one point, “Why are you treating cataracts only with a totally obsolete cataract operation?” And the man said to me, “Charlie, it’s such a wonderful operation to teach.” When he stopped using that operation, it was because almost all the patients had voted with their feet. Again, appeal to interest and not to reason if you want to change conclusions.

我在加州大学洛杉矶分校（UCLA）的朱尔斯·斯坦因眼科研究所（Jules Stein Eye Institute）也见过同样的事。有一次我问：“你们为什么只用一种完全过时的白内障手术326Cataract operation白内障手术来治疗？”那人对我说：“查理，这种手术教起来可太好了。”他后来不再用那种手术，是因为几乎所有可能的病人都用脚投了反对票。再一次说明，如果你想改变结论，要诉诸利益，而非诉诸理性。

Well, Berkshire’s whole record has been achieved without paying one ounce of attention to the efficient-market theory in its hard form, and not one ounce of attention to the descendants of that idea, which came out of academic economics and went into corporate finance and morphed into such obscenities as the capital asset pricing model, which we also paid no attention to. I think you’d have to believe in the tooth fairy327The Tooth Fairy牙仙 to believe that you could easily outperform the market by 7 percentage points per annum just by investing in high-volatility stocks.

嗯，伯克希尔的全部业绩，是在毫不理会那种僵化有效市场理论的情况下取得的，也毫不理会该理论在学院派经济学中衍生、后来进入公司理财、并异化成诸如资本资产定价模型这类荒谬东西的后代学说，这些我们也一概不理。我想，你若真相信只要投资高波动性股票就能每年轻松跑赢市场七个百分点，那你恐怕得相信牙仙327The Tooth Fairy牙仙才行。

Yet, believe it or not, like the Jules Stein doctor, people once believed this stuff. And the belief was rewarded, and it spread. And many people still believe it. But Berkshire never paid any attention to it. Now I think the world is coming our way, and the idea of perfection in all market outcomes is going the way of the dodo.

然而信不信由你，就像朱尔斯·斯坦因那位医生一样，人们一度相信这套东西。这种信念得到了回报，于是传播开来。许多人至今仍相信它。但伯克希尔从未理会过。现在我认为，世界正在转向我们这边，而“所有市场结果都完美”这种观点，正像渡渡鸟一样走向灭绝。

It was always clear to me that the stock market couldn’t be perfectly efficient, because as a teenager I’d been to the racetrack in Omaha, where they had the pari-mutuel system.328Pari-mutuel system同注分彩系统（赛马投注） And it was quite obvious to me that if the house take, the croupier’s take, was 17 percent, some people consistently lost a lot less than 17 percent of all their bets and other people consistently lost more than 17 percent of all their bets. So the pari-mutuel system in Omaha had no perfect efficiency, so I didn’t accept the argument that the stock market was always perfectly efficient in creating rational prices.

我一直都很清楚，股市不可能完全有效，因为我十几岁时去过奥马哈（Omaha）的赛马场，那里用的是彩池投注系统。我相当清楚地看到，如果庄家的抽成——也就是荷官的抽成——是17%，那么有些人每次下注输掉的钱始终远少于全部赌注的17%，而另一些人则始终多于17%。所以奥马哈的彩池投注系统并不完美有效，因此我不接受“股市在形成理性价格方面永远完全有效”这种说法。

Indeed, there have been some documented cases since of people getting so good at understanding horses and odds that they actually are able to beat the house in offtrack betting. There aren’t many people who can do that, but there are a few people in America who can.

事实上，后来有记录在案的例子表明，有些人把马匹和赔率研究得极其透彻，以至于真能在场外投注中战胜庄家。能做到这一点的人不多，但美国确实有那么几个。

Next, my personal education history is interesting because its deficiencies and my peculiarities eventually created advantages. For some odd reason, I had an early and extreme multidisciplinary cast of mind. I couldn’t stand reaching for a small idea in my own discipline when there was a big idea right over the fence in somebody else’s discipline. So I just grabbed in all directions for the big ideas that would really work. Nobody taught me to do that; I was just born with that yen.

接下来，我个人的教育经历很有意思，因为它的缺陷和我性格的怪癖最终变成了优势。出于某种奇怪的原因，我很早就有了一种极端的多学科思维倾向。当篱笆那边的别的学科里就有大思想时，我无法忍受在自己学科里只够得着一个小想法。于是我四面八方地去抓那些真正管用的大思想。没人教我这么做，我就是天生有这种渴望。

I also was born with a huge craving for synthesis. And when it didn’t come easily, which was often, I would rag the problem, and then, when I failed, I would put it aside, and I’d come back to it and rag it again. It took me 20 years to figure out how and why cult conversion methods worked. But the psychology departments haven’t figured it out yet, so I’m ahead of them.329Physics物理学

我还天生极度渴望综合。当综合来得不容易时——这经常发生——我会死磕这个问题，失败后就把它搁在一边，然后再回来继续死磕。我花了20年才搞明白邪教皈依方法是如何以及为何奏效的。但心理学系至今还没搞明白，所以我走在了他们前面。

But anyway, I have this tendency to want to rag the problems. Because WWII caught me, I drifted into some physics, and the Air Corps sent me to Caltech, where I did a little more physics as part of being made into a meteorologist. And there, at a very young age, I absorbed what I call the fundamental full attribution ethos of hard science. That was enormously useful to me. Let me explain that ethos.

但不管怎样，我有这种想要死磕问题的倾向。因为二战把我卷了进去，我偶然接触了一些物理学329Physics物理学，空军把我送到加州理工学院（Caltech，即 California Institute of Technology），在那里作为培养气象员的一部分，我又学了一点物理。就在那里，在很年轻的时候，我吸收了我所谓的硬科学“全归因治学精神”。这对我极其有用。让我来解释这种精神。

Under this ethos, you’ve got to know all the big ideas in all the disciplines more fundamental than your own. You can never make any explanation that can be made in a more fundamental way in any other way than the most fundamental way. And you always take them with full attribution to the most fundamental ideas that you are required to use. When you’re using physics, you say you’re using physics. When you’re using biology,330Biology生物学 you say you’re using biology. And so on and so on. I could early see that that ethos would act as a fine organizing system for my thought. And I strongly suspected that it would work really well in the soft sciences as well as the hard sciences, so I just grabbed it and used it all through my life in soft science as well as hard science. That was a very lucky idea for me.

在这种精神下，你必须掌握所有比自己学科更基础的其他学科里的大思想。任何可以用更基础的方式作出的解释，你绝不能以任何其他方式来解释。而且你总要完整地注明出处，标明你所用到的最基础的思想。你用物理学329Physics物理学时，就说你在用物理学；用生物学330Biology生物学时，就说你在用生物学。以此类推。我很早就看出，这种精神会是我的思想极好的组织系统。我强烈怀疑它在软科学中和在硬科学中一样好用，于是我抓住它，终生用于软科学和硬科学。这对我是个非常幸运的想法。

你必须掌握所有比自己学科更基础的其他学科里的大思想。

“You’ve got to know all the big ideas in all the disciplines more fundamental than your own.”你必须了解所有比自己学科更基础的其他学科里那些重要思想。

Let me explain how extreme that ethos is in hard science. There is a constant, one of the fundamental constants in physics, known as Boltzmann’s constant.331Boltzmann’s constantBoltzmann’s constant derives its name from Austrian physicist Ludwig Boltzmann (1844–1906); it defines the relation between absolute temperature and the kinetic energy contained in each molecule of an ideal gas. In general, the energy in a gas molecule is directly proportional to the absolute temperature. As the temperature increases, the kinetic energy per molecule increases. As a gas is heated, its molecules move more rapidly. This movement produces increased pressure if the gas is confined in a space of constant volume, or increased volume if the pressure remains constant.玻尔兹曼常数（Boltzmann's constant）以奥地利物理学家路德维希·玻尔兹曼（Ludwig Boltzmann，1844–1906 年）命名；它定义了绝对温度与理想气体每个分子所含动能之间的关系。一般而言，气体分子中的能量与绝对温度成正比。温度升高，每个分子的动能就增加。气体受热时，其分子运动得更快。如果气体被限制在恒定体积的空间里，这种运动会产生更大的压强；如果压强保持不变，则会产生更大的体积。 You probably all know it very well. The interesting thing about Boltzmann’s constant is that [Ludwig] Boltzmann332Ludwig Boltzmann路德维希·玻尔兹曼 didn’t discover it. So why is Boltzmann’s constant now named for Boltzmann? Well, the answer is that Boltzmann derived that constant from basic physics in a more fundamental way than the poor forgotten fellow who found the constant in the first place in some less fundamental way.

让我解释一下这种精神在硬科学中有多极端。物理学中有一个常数，是物理学的基本常数之一，叫做波尔茨曼常数（Boltzmann's constant）。你们大概都很熟悉。关于波尔茨曼常数有趣的是，发现它的并不是波尔茨曼。那么为什么波尔茨曼常数现在以波尔茨曼命名呢？答案是，比起那位最先以较不基础的方式发现这个常数的、已被遗忘的可怜人，波尔茨曼用更基础的方式从基础物理学中推导出了这个常数。

The ethos of hard science is so strong in favor of reductionism to the more fundamental body of knowledge that you can wash the discoverer right out of history when somebody else handles his discovery in a more fundamental way. I think that is correct. I think Boltzmann’s constant should be named for Boltzmann.

硬科学的精神如此强烈地偏向还原到更基础的知识体系，以至于当别人以更基础的方式处理某项发现时，你完全可以把最初的发现者从历史上洗刷掉。我认为这没错。我认为波尔茨曼常数就该以波尔茨曼命名。

当别人以更基础的方式处理某项发现时，你完全可以把最初的发现者从历史上洗刷掉。

“You can wash the discoverer right out of history when somebody else handles his discovery in a more fundamental way.”当别人以更基础的方式运用某项发现时，你完全可以把发现者从历史中抹掉。

At any rate, in my history and Berkshire’s history, Berkshire went on and on into considerable economic success while ignoring the hard-form efficient-markets doctrine once very popular in academic economics and ignoring the descendants of that doctrine in corporate finance, where the results became even sillier than they were in economics. This naturally encouraged me.

无论如何，在我和伯克希尔的历史中，伯克希尔无视一度在学院派经济学中极流行的僵化有效市场教条，也无视该教条在公司理财中的衍生学说——后者的结果比经济学中还要荒唐——却一路取得了相当的经济成功。这自然鼓舞了我。

Finally, with my peculiar history, I’m also bold enough to be here today because, at least when I was young, I wasn’t a total klutz. For one year at the Harvard Law School, I was ranked second in a very large group, and I always figured that, while there were always a lot of people much smarter than I was, I didn’t have to hang back totally in the thinking game.333Adam Smith亚当·斯密

最后，凭借我这特殊的经历，我今天也够胆站在这里，因为至少在我年轻时，我并非彻头彻尾的笨蛋。在哈佛法学院（Harvard Law School）的那一年，我在很大一个群体里排名第二，而我一向认为，尽管总有许多人比我聪明得多，但在思维这场游戏里，我不必完全退缩。

Let me begin by discussing the obvious strengths of academic economics. The first obvious strength—and this is true of a lot of places that get repute—is that it was in the right place at the right time. Two hundred years ago, aided by the growth of technology and the growth of other developments in civilization, the real output per capita of the civilized world started going up at about 2 percent per annum, compounded. Before that, for the previous thousands of years, it had gone up at a rate that hovered just a hair’s breadth above zero. And, of course, economics grew up amid this huge success. Partly it helped the success, and partly it explained it. So, naturally, academic economics grew. And lately, with the collapse of all the communist economies, as the free-market economies or partially free-market economies flourished, that added to the reputation of economics. Economics has been a very favorable place to be if you’re in academia.

让我先来谈学院派经济学那些明显的长处。第一个明显的长处——许多获得声誉的学科也是如此——是它生逢其时、生逢其地。两百年前，在技术发展和文明其他方面进步的助推下，文明世界的人均实际产出开始以每年约2%的复合增长率上升。在此之前的数千年里，它的增速一直紧贴零的上方徘徊。当然，经济学正是在这种巨大成功中成长起来的。它部分促成了这种成功，部分解释了这种成功。于是，学院派经济学自然就发展壮大了。近来，随着所有计划经济的崩溃，自由市场经济或半自由市场经济蓬勃发展，这又增添了经济学的声望。如果你在学术界，经济学是个非常吃香的去处。

Economics was always more multidisciplinary than the rest of soft science. It just reached out and grabbed things as it needed to. And that tendency to just grab whatever you need from the rest of knowledge if you’re an economist has reached a fairly high point in N. Gregory Mankiw ’s334N. Gregory MankiwN. Gregory Mankiw (b. 1958) studied economics at Princeton University, earned a PhD from MIT, and is on the faculty at Harvard University. In 2003, he was appointed chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers.N. 格里高利·曼昆（N. Gregory Mankiw，1958 年生）在普林斯顿大学学习经济学，从麻省理工学院获得博士学位，现为哈佛大学教师。2003 年，他获任经济顾问委员会（Council of Economic Advisers）主席。 new textbook.

经济学向来比其他软科学更跨学科。它只是伸手去抓取它所需要的东西。而“只要是经济学家，就从其他知识里抓取所需”这种倾向，在格里高利·曼昆334N. Gregory MankiwN. Gregory Mankiw (b. 1958) studied economics at Princeton University, earned a PhD from MIT, and is on the faculty at Harvard University. In 2003, he was appointed chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers.N. 格里高利·曼昆（N. Gregory Mankiw，1958 年生）在普林斯顿大学学习经济学，从麻省理工学院获得博士学位，现为哈佛大学教师。2003 年，他获任经济顾问委员会（Council of Economic Advisers）主席。（N. Gregory Mankiw）的新教材里达到了一个相当高的高度。

I checked out that textbook. I must have been one of the few businessmen in America who bought it immediately when it came out because it had gotten such a big advance. I wanted to figure out what the guy was doing where he could get an advance that great. So this is how I happened to riffle through Mankiw’s freshman textbook. And there I found laid out as principles of economics: Opportunity cost is a superpower, to be used by all people who have any hope of getting the right answer. Also, incentives are superpowers. And lastly, the tragedy of the commons model, popularized by my longtime friend, UCSB’s Garrett Hardin.335Garrett HardinGarrett Hardin (1915–2003) , born in Dallas, spent his childhood in the Midwest. He earned an undergraduate degree from the University of Chicago and a PhD in biology from Stanford University. In 1946, he joined the faculty at UC Santa Barbara. His essay “The Tragedy of the Commons” became a staple of ecological thought. His philosophical and political positions influenced debates on abortion, immigration, foreign aid, and other issues for decades.加勒特·哈丁（Garrett Hardin，1915–2003 年）生于达拉斯，在中西部长大。他从芝加哥大学获得本科学位，又从斯坦福大学获得生物学博士学位。1946 年，他加入加州大学圣巴巴拉分校教师队伍。他的文章《公地的悲剧》（The Tragedy of the Commons）成了生态学思想的基本读物。他的哲学和政治立场影响了此后数十年关于堕胎、移民、对外援助等议题的争论。 Hardin caused the delightful introduction into economics, alongside Smith’s336Adam SmithAdam Smith recorded in An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations (1776) his observations at a pin factory. He found that only 10 workers were able to produce 48,000 pins per day because of divided and specialized labor. If each worker handled all the steps required to make a pin, he could only make 20 per day, for a total factory output of 200 pins daily. Smith recognized and extolled the great productivity gains and economic progress represented by the pin factory and its embrace of specialized labor.亚当·斯密在《国富论》（An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations，1776 年）中记录了他对一家别针工厂的观察。他发现，由于分工和专业化劳动，仅 10 名工人每天就能生产 48,000 枚别针。如果每个工人亲手完成制作一枚别针所需的全部工序，他每天只能做 20 枚，全厂日产量只有 200 枚。斯密认识到并赞扬了别针工厂及其对专业化劳动的拥抱所代表的巨大生产率提升和经济进步。 beneficent invisible hand, of Hardin’s wicked, evildoing invisible foot. Well, I thought that the Hardin model made economics more complete, and I knew when Hardin introduced me to his model, the tragedy of the commons, that it would be in the economics textbooks eventually. And lo and behold, it finally made it about 20 years later. And it’s right for Mankiw to reach out into other disciplines and grab Hardin’s model, and anything else that works well.

我翻了翻那本教材。我肯定是美国少数几个一出版就买的商人之一，因为它拿了一大笔预付稿酬。我想弄清楚那家伙凭什么能拿到那么高的预付。所以我就是这样偶然翻了翻曼昆给大一新生写的教材。在那里我看到了被列作经济学原理的几点：机会成本是超级力量，所有有望得到正确答案的人都应使用它。还有，激励是超级力量。最后，是公地悲剧模型，由我的老朋友、加州大学圣塔巴巴拉分校（UCSB）的加勒特·哈丁335Garrett HardinGarrett Hardin (1915–2003) , born in Dallas, spent his childhood in the Midwest. He earned an undergraduate degree from the University of Chicago and a PhD in biology from Stanford University. In 1946, he joined the faculty at UC Santa Barbara. His essay “The Tragedy of the Commons” became a staple of ecological thought. His philosophical and political positions influenced debates on abortion, immigration, foreign aid, and other issues for decades.加勒特·哈丁（Garrett Hardin，1915–2003 年）生于达拉斯，在中西部长大。他从芝加哥大学获得本科学位，又从斯坦福大学获得生物学博士学位。1946 年，他加入加州大学圣巴巴拉分校教师队伍。他的文章《公地的悲剧》（The Tragedy of the Commons）成了生态学思想的基本读物。他的哲学和政治立场影响了此后数十年关于堕胎、移民、对外援助等议题的争论。（Garrett Hardin）推广开来。哈丁把一只邪恶作祟的无形之脚引入了经济学，与斯密333Adam Smith亚当·斯密那只仁慈的无形之手并列。嗯，我认为哈丁的模型让经济学更完整了，而且当哈丁向我介绍他的公地悲剧模型时，我就知道它迟早会写进经济学教材。瞧，大约20年后它终于进去了。曼昆伸手从其他学科抓取哈丁的模型以及任何其他管用的东西，这是对的。

Another thing that helped economics is that, from the beginning, it attracted the best brains in soft science. Its denizens also interacted more with the practical world than was at all common in soft science and the rest of academia, and that resulted in very creditable outcomes like the three Cabinet appointments of economics PhD George Shultz337George ShultzGeorge Shultz (1920–2021) , born in New York City, earned an undergraduate degree in economics from Princeton University and a PhD in industrial economics at MIT. Following several years on the MIT faculty, he moved on to the University of Chicago. He served as President Richard M. Nixon’s secretary of the treasury for two years until Nixon was forced to resign. President Ronald Reagan appointed him secretary of state in 1982; Shultz served both of Reagan’s terms. He is a member of the Hoover Institution and on the board of directors for the Bechtel Corporation, Gilead Sciences, and Charles Schwab & Company. During Arnold Schwarzenegger’s successful bid to replace California governor Gray Davis in 2003, Shultz was named an adviser to Schwarzenegger’s campaign.乔治·舒尔茨（George Shultz，1920–2021 年）生于纽约市，从普林斯顿大学获得经济学本科学位，又在麻省理工学院获得产业经济学博士学位。在麻省理工学院任教数年后，他转往芝加哥大学。他担任理查德·M·尼克松总统的财政部长两年，直到尼克松被迫辞职。罗纳德·里根总统 1982 年任命他为国务卿；舒尔茨干满了里根的两个任期。他是胡佛研究所成员，并担任贝泰公司（Bechtel）、吉利德科学（Gilead Sciences）和嘉信理财（Charles Schwab & Company）的董事。2003 年阿诺德·施瓦辛格成功竞选取代加州州长格雷·戴维斯期间，舒尔茨被任命为施瓦辛格竞选团队的顾问。 and the Cabinet appointment of Larry Summers. So this has been a very favored part of academia.

另一件帮了经济学的事是，从一开始，它就吸引了软科学中最聪明的大脑。它的从业者也比软科学及学术界其他领域的人更普遍地与实际世界互动，这带来了非常值得称道的成果，比如经济学博士乔治·舒尔茨377George Shultz乔治·舒尔茨（George Shultz）三次入阁，以及拉里·萨默斯（Larry Summers）入阁任职。所以这一直是学术界颇受青睐的领域。

Also, economics early on attracted some of the best writers of language in the history of the earth. You start out with. Adam Smith was so good a thinker and so good a writer that, in his own time, Immanuel Kant,339Immanuel Kant伊曼努尔·康德 then the greatest intellectual in Germany, simply announced that there was nobody in Germany to equal Adam Smith. Well, Voltaire,340Voltaire伏尔泰 being an even pithier speaker than Kant, which wouldn’t be that hard, immediately said, “Oh, well, France doesn’t have anybody who can even be compared to Adam Smith.”

此外，经济学很早还吸引了地球上历史上一些最杰出的语言大师。你们从亚当·斯密333Adam Smith亚当·斯密（Adam Smith）说起。亚当·斯密既是极好的思想家，又是极好的作家，以至于在他那个时代，当时德国最伟大的学者伊曼努尔·康德339Immanuel Kant伊曼努尔·康德（Emmanuel Kant）干脆宣称，德国没有人比得上亚当·斯密。而伏尔泰340Voltaire伏尔泰（Voltaire）说话比康德更精炼——这倒也不难——立刻说：“哦，法国根本没有人能跟亚当·斯密相提并论。”

So economics started with some very great men and great writers. And then there have been later great writers like John Maynard Keynes,341John Maynard KeynesJohn Maynard Keynes (1883–1946) , son of an economics lecturer at Cambridge University and a social reformist, seemed destined to become a great economist and political thinker. His book, The General Theory of Employment, Interest, and Money , published in 1936, advocated that government stimulate demand in times of high unemployment—for example, by spending on public works. The book serves as the foundation of modern macroeconomics.约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯（John Maynard Keynes，1883–1946 年）是剑桥大学一位经济学讲师和社会改革论者之子，似乎注定要成为伟大的经济学家和政治思想家。他 1936 年出版的著作《就业、利息和货币通论》（The General Theory of Employment, Interest, and Money）主张，在高失业时期政府应刺激需求，例如通过公共工程支出。该书是现代宏观经济学的基石。 whom I quote all the time and who has added a great amount of illumination to my life. And finally, even in the present era, if you take Paul Krugman342Paul Krugman保罗·克鲁格曼 and read his essays, you will be impressed by his fluency. I can’t stand his politics; I’m on the other side. But I love this man’s essays. I think Paul Krugman is one of the best essayists alive. So economics has constantly attracted these fabulous writers. And they are so good that they have this enormous influence far outside their economic discipline, and that’s very uncommon in other academic departments.

所以经济学起步于一些非常伟大的人物和伟大的作家。后来又有约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯363John Maynard Keynes约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯（John Maynard Keynes）这样的伟大作家，我总引用他，他为我的生活增添了大量启发。最后，即使在当代，如果你读保罗·克鲁格曼342Paul Krugman保罗·克鲁格曼（Paul Krugman）的随笔，也会折服于他的文笔流畅。我受不了他的政治立场；我站在另一边。但我喜欢这个人的随笔。我认为保罗·克鲁格曼是当今在世最优秀的随笔作家之一。所以经济学不断吸引这些了不起的作家。他们如此出色，以至于其巨大影响远远超出经济学学科，这在其他学术系所里很少见。

Okay, now it’s time to extend criticism instead of praise. We’ve recognized that economics is better than other soft science academic departments in many ways, and one of the glories of civilization. Now it’s only fair that we outline a few things that are wrong with academic economics.

好，现在是时候展开批评而非赞美了。我们已经承认，经济学在许多方面都优于其他软科学系所，是文明的荣耀之一。现在，公平起见，我们该列举学院派经济学的一些不妥之处。

OneFatal unconnectedness, leading to man-with-a-hammer syndrome, often causing overweighing of what can be counted

I think I’ve got eight—no, nine—objections, some being logical subdivisions of a big general objection. The big general objection to economics was the one early described by Alfred North Whitehead343Alfred North WhiteheadAlfred North Whitehead (1861–1947) , a British philosopher and mathematician, worked in logic, mathematics, philosophy of science, and metaphysics. Whitehead is known for developing process philosophy, a view holding that fundamental elements of the universe are occasions of experience. In this view, concrete objects are actually successions of these occasions of experience. By grouping occasions of experience, something as complex as a human being can be defined. Whitehead’s views evolved into process theology, a way of understanding God. His best-known mathematics work is Principia Mathematica , co-written with Bertrand Russell.阿尔弗雷德·诺斯·怀特海（Alfred North Whitehead，1861–1947 年）是英国哲学家和数学家，研究逻辑、数学、科学哲学和形而上学。怀特海以发展过程哲学闻名，该观点认为宇宙的基本元素是“经验的机缘”。依此观点，具体的对象实际上是这些经验机缘的延续。通过对经验机缘加以分组，诸如人类这样复杂的事物也能得到定义。怀特海的观点后来演化为过程神学，一种理解上帝的方式。他最著名的数学著作是与伯特兰·罗素（Bertrand Russell）合著的《数学原理》（Principia Mathematica）。 when he spoke of the fatal unconnectedness of academic disciplines, wherein each professor didn’t even know the models of the other disciplines, much less try to synthesize those disciplines with his own. I think there’s a modern name for this approach that Whitehead didn’t like, and that name is “bonkers.” This is a perfectly crazy way to behave. Yet economics, like much else in academia, is too insular.

我想我有八个——不对，是九个——反对意见，其中一些是某个大总体反对意见的逻辑分支。对经济学那个大的总体反对意见，最早由阿尔弗雷德·诺斯·怀特海343Alfred North WhiteheadAlfred North Whitehead (1861–1947) , a British philosopher and mathematician, worked in logic, mathematics, philosophy of science, and metaphysics. Whitehead is known for developing process philosophy, a view holding that fundamental elements of the universe are occasions of experience. In this view, concrete objects are actually successions of these occasions of experience. By grouping occasions of experience, something as complex as a human being can be defined. Whitehead’s views evolved into process theology, a way of understanding God. His best-known mathematics work is Principia Mathematica , co-written with Bertrand Russell.阿尔弗雷德·诺斯·怀特海（Alfred North Whitehead，1861–1947 年）是英国哲学家和数学家，研究逻辑、数学、科学哲学和形而上学。怀特海以发展过程哲学闻名，该观点认为宇宙的基本元素是“经验的机缘”。依此观点，具体的对象实际上是这些经验机缘的延续。通过对经验机缘加以分组，诸如人类这样复杂的事物也能得到定义。怀特海的观点后来演化为过程神学，一种理解上帝的方式。他最著名的数学著作是与伯特兰·罗素（Bertrand Russell）合著的《数学原理》（Principia Mathematica）。（Alfred North Whitehead）提出，他谈到各学术学科之间致命的互不连通，每个教授甚至不了解其他学科的模型，更别说试着把这些学科与自己的综合起来。我认为怀特海不喜欢的这种做法有个现代名称，叫“bonkers”（脑子坏掉）。这完全是发疯的行为方式。然而经济学和学术界许多其他领域一样，太过封闭。

怀特海不喜欢的这种做法有个现代名称，叫“bonkers”（脑子坏掉）。

“There’s a modern name for this approach that Whitehead didn’t like, and that name is ‘bonkers.’”怀特海（Whitehead）不喜欢的这种做派，如今有个名字，叫『疯癫』（bonkers）。

The nature of this failure is that it creates what I always call man-with-a-hammer syndrome. That’s taken from the folk saying “To the man with only a hammer, every problem looks pretty much like a nail.”344The man with only a hammer只有锤子的人 That works marvelously to gum up all professions and all departments of academia and, indeed, most practical life.

这种失败的本质在于，它造成了我所谓的“手里拿锤子的人”综合症。这取自那句俗话：“手里只有一把锤子的人，看每个问题都差不多像颗钉子。”这极善于把各行各业、各学术系所，乃至大部分实际生活，搅成一团糟。

The only antidote for being an absolute klutz due to the presence of a man-with-a-hammer syndrome is to have a full kit of tools. You don’t have just a hammer, you’ve got all the tools. And you’ve got to have one more trick: You’ve got to use those tools checklist-style,345Checklist检查清单 because you’ll miss a lot if you just hope that the right tool is going to pop up unaided whenever you need it. But if you’ve got a full list of tools and go through them in your mind, checklist-style, you will find a lot of answers that you won’t find any other way. So limiting this big general objection that so disturbed Alfred North Whitehead is very important, and there are mental tricks that help do the job.

因“手里拿锤子的人”综合症而成为彻头彻尾笨蛋的唯一解药，是拥有一整套工具。你不该只有一把锤子，而该拥有所有工具。而且你还得多一招：你必须像核对清单那样使用这些工具，因为如果你只是指望需要时合适的工具会自动冒出来，你会漏掉很多。但如果你有一份完整的工具清单，并在脑中逐一过一遍，像清单那样，你就会找到许多用其他方法找不到的答案。所以，抑制这个让阿尔弗雷德·诺斯·怀特海如此不安的大总体反对意见非常重要，而有些思维窍门能帮上忙。

A special version of this man-with-a-hammer syndrome is terrible not only in economics but practically everywhere else, including business. It’s really terrible in business. You’ve got a complex system, and it spews out a lot of wonderful numbers that enable you to measure some factors. But there are other factors that are terribly important, yet there’s no precise numbering you can put to these factors. You know they’re important, but you don’t have the numbers. Well, practically everybody 1) overweighs the stuff that can be numbered because it yields to the statistical techniques they’re taught in academia and 2) doesn’t mix in the hard-to-measure stuff that may be more important. That is a mistake I’ve tried all my life to avoid, and I have no regrets for having done that.

这种“手里拿锤子的人”综合症的特别版本，不仅在经济学中很可怕，在几乎所有其他地方——包括商业——都一样。在商业中它真的很可怕。你有一个复杂系统，它吐出大量漂亮数字，让你能量化某些因素。但还有其他极其重要的因素，你却无法精确赋数。你知道它们重要，却拿不到数字。于是， practically 每个人都：1）高估那些可量化的东西，因为它们能套上学界教给的统计技巧；2）不把那些更难量化、却可能更重要的东西纳入考量。这是我毕生努力避免的错误，我对此毫无悔意。

The late, great Thomas Hunt Morgan,346Thomas Hunt Morgan托马斯·亨特·摩根 who was one of the greatest biologists who ever lived, when he got to Caltech had a very interesting, extreme way of avoiding some mistakes from overcounting what could be measured and undercounting what couldn’t. At that time, there were no computers, and the computer substitute then available to science and engineering was the Friden calculator,347Friden calculator弗里登计算器 and Caltech was full of Friden calculators. Thomas Hunt Morgan banned the Friden calculator from the biology department. And when they said, “What the hell are you doing, Dr. Morgan?,” he said, “Well, I am like a guy who is prospecting for gold348Prospecting for gold探金 along the banks of the Sacramento River in 1849. With a little intelligence, I can reach down and pick up big nuggets of gold. And as long as I can do that, I’m not going to let any people in my department waste scarce resources in placer mining.”349Placer miningFar less efficient than Munger’s preferred approach of simply “reaching down and picking up big nuggets of gold,” placer mining (pronounced “plass-er”) is an open-pit or open-cast form of mining in which miniscule amounts of valuable minerals are extracted from great volumes of earth using water pressure or surface excavating equipment. The name derives from the Spanish word , meaning “sand bank,” and refers to precious metal deposits (particularly gold and gemstones) found in alluvial deposits.比起芒格偏爱的“俯身捡起大金块”那种方式，砂矿开采（placer mining，读作“plass-er”）效率要低得多，它是一种露天开采形式，用水压或表面挖掘设备从巨量泥土中提取微量的有价值矿物。该名称源自西班牙语，意为“沙洲”，指在冲积层中发现的贵金属（尤其是金和宝石）矿床。 And that’s the way Thomas Hunt Morgan got through life.

已故的伟人托马斯·亨特·摩根346Thomas Hunt Morgan托马斯·亨特·摩根（Thomas Hunt Morgan）是有史以来最伟大的生物学家之一，他到加州理工学院后，用了一种非常有趣而极端的办法，来避免某些错误——即高估可测量之物、低估不可测量之物。那时没有计算机，科学与工程界可用的计算机替代品是弗里登计算器347Friden calculator弗里登计算器（Friden calculator），加州理工学院到处都是弗里登计算器。托马斯·亨特·摩根禁止生物系使用弗里登计算器。当他们问“摩根博士，你到底在搞什么鬼”时，他说：“嗯，我就像1849年在萨克拉门托河（Sacramento River）岸边淘金的人。凭一点聪明，我就能弯腰捡起大金块。只要我能这么干，我就不会让我系里的人浪费稀缺资源去淘沙金。”托马斯·亨特·摩根就是这样度过一生的。

I’ve adopted the same technique, and here I am in my 80th year. I haven’t had to do any placer mining yet. And it begins to look like I’m going to get all the way through, as I’d always hoped, without doing any of that damned placer mining. Of course, if I were a physician, particularly an academic physician, I’d have to do the statistics, do the placer mining. But it’s amazing what you can do in life without the placer mining if you’ve got a few good mental tricks and just keep ragging the problems the way Thomas Hunt Morgan did.

我采用了同样的办法，如今我已是八旬之人。我至今没做过任何淘沙金的事。而且看来，正如我一直希望的那样，我大概率能一路走到头，而不必做那种该死的淘沙金。当然，如果我是医生，尤其是学院派医生，我就得做统计，得去淘沙金。但如果你有几个好用的思维窍门，并且像托马斯·亨特·摩根那样不断死磕问题，那么生活中不淘沙金却能做成的事，会让人惊叹。

如果你有几个好用的思维窍门，并不断死磕问题，那么生活中不淘沙金却能做成的事，会让人惊叹。

“It’s amazing what you can do in life without the placer mining if you’ve got a few good mental tricks and just keep ragging the problems.”只要你掌握几招管用的心智技巧，并且不停地去折腾那些问题，你会发现，不靠淘砂挖金（placer mining），人生照样能做成许多事，实在惊人。
TwoFailure to follow the fundamental full-attribution ethos of hard science

What’s wrong with the way Mankiw does economics is that he grabs from other disciplines without attribution. He doesn’t label the grabbed items as physics or biology or psychology or game theory or whatever they really are, fully attributing the concept to the basic knowledge from which it came. If you don’t do that, it’s like running a business with a sloppy filing system. It reduces your power to be as good as you can be.

曼昆做经济学的不对之处在于，他从其他学科抓取却不注明出处。他没有把抓来的东西贴上物理学、生物学、心理学、博弈论或它们真正所属的任何学科的标签，没有把概念完整地归功到它源自的基础知识。如果你不这么做，那就好比用一套糟糕的归档系统经营企业。它会削弱你做到最好的能力。

Now, Mankiw is so smart he does pretty well even when his technique is imperfect. He got the largest advance any textbook writer ever got. But nonetheless, he’d be better if he had absorbed a hard-science ethos, which has been helpful to me.

不过，曼昆如此聪明，即便方法不完善也做得相当好。他拿到了任何教科书作者都拿过的最高预付稿酬。但尽管如此，如果他吸收了硬科学的精神——这对我很有帮助——他会做得更好。

I have names for Mankiw’s approach, grabbing whatever you need without attribution. Sometimes I call it “take what you wish,” and sometimes I call it “Kiplingism.” And when I call it Kiplingism, I’m reminding you of [Joseph Rudyard] Kipling’s350Joseph Rudyard KiplingJoseph Rudyard Kipling (1865–1936) , born in Bombay, India, to a father who taught at a local art school, attended boarding school in England. He returned to India and traveled around the subcontinent as a correspondent. He also wrote fiction and poetry, publishing The Jungle Book in 1894, Captains Courageous in 1897, and “Gunga Din” in 1892. Well, that’s the way Mankiw does it. He just grabs. This is much better than not grabbing. But it is much worse than grabbing with full attribution and full discipline, using all knowledge plus extreme reductionism where feasible.

ThreePhysics envy

The third weakness that I find in economics is what I call physics envy. And, of course, that term has been borrowed from “penis envy,” as described by one of the world’s great idiots, Sigmund Freud. But he was very popular in his time, and the concept got a wide vogue.

我在经济学中发现的第三个弱点是所谓的“物理学妒忌”。当然，这个词借自“阴茎妒忌”，由世界上最伟大的白痴之一西格蒙德·弗洛伊德（Sigmund Freud）所描述。但他在那个时代极受欢迎，这个概念也广为流行。

One of the worst examples of what physics envy did to economics was cause adoption of hard-form efficient-market theory. Then, when you logically derived consequences from this wrong theory, you would get conclusions such as it can never be correct for any corporation to buy its own stock. Because the stock price, by definition, is totally efficient, there could never be any advantage, QED. But he so believed what he’d been taught in graduate school that he told The Washington Post it shouldn’t buy its own stock.

Well, fortunately, they put Warren Buffett on the board, and he convinced them to buy back more than half of the outstanding stock, which enriched the remaining shareholders by much more than a billion dollars. So there was at least one instance of a place that quickly killed a wrong academic theory.

嗯，幸运的是，他们让沃伦·巴菲特进了董事会，他说服他们回购了超过一半的流通股，让剩余股东凭空多出了十多亿美元的财富。所以至少曾有一个地方迅速杀死了一个错误的学术理论。

It’s my view that economics could avoid a lot of this trouble that comes from physics envy. I want economics to pick up the basic ethos of hard science, the full attribution habit, but not the craving for an unattainable precision that comes from physics envy. The sort of precise, reliable formula that includes Boltzmann’s constant is not going to happen, by and large, in economics. Economics involves too complex a system. And the craving for that physics-style precision does little but get you in terrible trouble, like the poor fool from McKinsey.

我认为经济学本可以避免许多由物理学妒忌带来的麻烦。我希望经济学拾起硬科学的基本精神、完整注明的习惯，但不要拾起由物理学妒忌而来的、对无法企及的精确性的渴望。那种包含波尔茨曼常数式的精确可靠公式，在经济学中大体上不会出现。经济学涉及的系统太复杂。而对那种物理学式精确性的渴望，除了让你陷入可怕的麻烦——就像麦肯锡那个可怜的傻瓜——几乎一无是处。

Sharon Stone contributed to the subject because someone once asked her if she was bothered by penis envy. And she said, “Absolutely not. I have more trouble than I can handle with what I’ve got.”

莎朗·斯通对这话题也有贡献，因为有人曾问她是否受阴茎妒忌困扰。她说：“绝对没有。我手头已有的这些东西，带给我的麻烦已经够我应付了。”

When I talk about this false precision, this great hope for reliable, precise formulas, I am reminded of Arthur Laffer,354Arthur Laffer阿瑟·拉弗 who’s in my political party, and who takes a mistaken approach, sometimes, when it comes to doing economics. His trouble is his craving for false precision, which is not an adult way of dealing with his subject matter.

当我谈到这种虚假的精确、这种对可靠精确公式的巨大期望时，我想起了阿瑟·拉弗（Arthur Laffer），354Arthur Laffer阿瑟·拉弗他与我同属一个政党，而在做经济学时，有时会采取错误的方法。他的麻烦在于渴望虚假的精确，那不是以成熟方式对待其研究对象的态度。

The situation of people like Laffer reminds me of a rustic legislator—and this really happened in America. I don’t invent these stories. Reality is always more ridiculous than what I’m going to tell you. At any rate, this rustic legislator proposed a new law in his state. He wanted to pass a law rounding pi to an even 3.2 so it would be easier for the schoolchildren to make the computations.

像拉弗这样的人的处境，让我想起一位乡巴佬立法者——这在美国真发生过。我不编造这些故事。现实总是比我接下来要讲的更荒唐。总之，这位乡巴佬立法者在他所在的州提出了一项新法律。他想通过一项法律，把圆周率π取整为规整的3.2，好让小学生计算起来更容易。

Well, you can say that this is too ridiculous, and it can’t be fair to liken economics professors like Laffer to a rustic legislator like this. I say I’m under-criticizing the professors. At least when this rustic legislator rounded pi to an even number, the error was relatively small. But once you try to put a lot of false precision into a complex system like economics, the errors can compound to the point where they’re worse than those of the McKinsey partner when he was incompetently advising The Washington Post. So economics should emulate physics’ basic ethos, but its search for precision in physics-like formulas is almost always wrong in economics.

嗯，你或许会说这太荒唐，把拉弗那样的经济学教授比作这样的乡巴佬立法者不公平。我说我是在轻描淡写地批评那些教授。至少这位乡巴佬立法者把π取整时，误差相对较小。可一旦你试图把大量虚假的精确塞进经济学这样的复杂系统，误差就会复利累积，糟糕到超过那位麦肯锡合伙人不称职地给《华盛顿邮报》当顾问时的程度。所以经济学应当效法物理学的基本精神，但它在物理学式公式中追求精确的做法，在经济学中几乎总是错的。

Test FourToo much emphasis on macroeconomics

My fourth criticism is that there’s too much emphasis on macroeconomics and not enough on microeconomics. I think this is wrong. It’s like trying to master medicine without knowing anatomy and chemistry. Also, the discipline of microeconomics is a lot of fun. It helps you correctly understand macroeconomics, and it’s a perfect circus to do. In contrast, I don’t think macroeconomics people have all that much fun. For one thing, they are often wrong because of extreme complexity in the system they wish to understand.

我的第四条批评是，经济学界太过强调宏观经济学，而对微观经济学重视不足。我认为这错了。这就像不懂解剖学和化学却想掌握医学。而且，微观经济学这门学问很有趣。它帮你正确理解宏观经济学，做起来像一场绝妙的马戏。相反，我认为研究宏观经济学的人并没那么多乐趣。原因之一在于，由于他们想理解的系统极度复杂，他们常常出错。

微观经济学这门学问很有趣。它帮你正确理解宏观经济学，做起来像一场绝妙的马戏。

“The discipline of microeconomics is a lot of fun. It helps you correctly understand macroeconomics, and it’s a perfect circus to do.”微观经济学这门学问很有意思。它能帮你正确地理解宏观经济学，而且钻研起来像一场绝佳的马戏。

Let me demonstrate the power of microeconomics by solving two microeconomic problems, one simple and one a little harder.

让我通过解决两个微观经济学问题来展示微观经济学的威力，一个简单，一个稍难。

The first problem is this: Berkshire Hathaway just opened a furniture and appliance store in Kansas City, Kansas. At the time Berkshire opened it, the largest-selling furniture and appliance store in the world was another Berkshire Hathaway store selling $350 million worth of goods per year. The new store in a strange city opened up selling at the rate of more than $500 million a year. From the day it opened, the 3,200 spaces in the parking lot were full. The women had to wait outside the ladies’ restroom because the architects didn’t understand biology. It’s hugely successful.

第一个问题是这样的：伯克希尔·哈撒韦刚在堪萨斯州（Kansas）的堪萨斯城（Kansas City）开了一家家具和家电店。伯克希尔开这家店时，全球销量最大的家具和家电店也是另一家伯克希尔·哈撒韦的店，年销售额3.5亿美元。这家开在陌生城市的新店，一开张就以每年超过5亿美元的速率销售。从开业那天起，停车场的3200个车位全满。女顾客不得不在女洗手间外排队，因为建筑师不懂生物学。它取得了巨大的成功。

Well, I’ve given you the problem. Now, tell me what explains the runaway success of this new furniture and appliance store that is outselling everything else in the world.

好，我已经把问题给了你们。现在，告诉我，这家新家具家电店何以能势不可挡地成功，销量超过全世界其他一切店铺。

Let me do it for you. Is this a low-priced store or a high-priced store? It’s not going to have runaway success in a strange city as a high-priced store. That would take time. Number two, if it’s moving $500 million worth of furniture through it, it’s one hell of a big store, furniture being as bulky as it is. And what does a big store do? It provides a big selection. So what could this possibly be except a low-priced store with a big selection?

让我替你们解答。这是一家低价店还是高价店？在陌生城市，高价店不可能一飞冲天。那需要时间。第二，如果它一年流转5亿美元的家具，那它绝对是个巨无霸商店，家具本来就很占地方。而大商店做的是什么？它提供海量选择。所以，除了“低价+海量选择”的商店，它还能是什么？

But you may wonder, why wasn’t it done before, preventing its being done first now? Again, the answer just pops into your head: It costs a fortune to open a store this big, so nobody’s done it before. So you quickly know the answer. With a few basic concepts, these microeconomic problems that seem hard can be solved much as you put a hot knife through butter. I like such easy ways of thought that are very remunerative. And I suggest that you people should also learn to do microeconomics better.

但你可能纳闷，为什么以前没人这么做，以至于现在才轮到它当第一？答案同样直接蹦进你脑海：开这么大的店要花一大笔钱，所以以前没人开过。于是你很快知道了答案。有了几个基本概念，这些看似困难的微观经济学问题就能像热刀切黄油一样解决。我喜欢这种轻松又回报丰厚的思维方式。我建议你们也应学会更好地做微观经济学。

In the 1950s, Schwab began expanding his business throughout the Pacific Northwest. Through innovations such as profit sharing, “supermarket” product selection, and independence from the tire manufacturing companies, the company now operates over 300 stores with sales exceeding $1 billion annually.莱斯·施瓦布（Les Schwab，1917–2007 年）生于俄勒冈州本德。二战期间在空军学员队服役后，他回到俄勒冈，买下了 OK Rubber Welders——一家小型轮胎店，并把它从年营业额 3.2 万美元的生意做成了年入 15 万美元。20 世纪 50 年代，施瓦布开始把生意扩展到整个太平洋西北地区。通过利润分享、“超市”式选品、以及不依赖轮胎制造商等创新，公司如今运营着 300 多家门店，年销售额超过 10 亿美元。（Les Schwab）轮胎连锁店。它只是一步一个脚印地往前走。它一开始与各大轮胎公司——即生产所有轮胎的固特异（Goodyears）等——自家的店竞争。当然，制造商偏袒自己的店。它们的“关联店”有巨大的成本优势。后来，勒斯·施瓦布在与好市多（Costco）、山姆会员店（Sam's Club）等巨型折扣商，以及更早的西尔斯·罗巴克（Sears, Roebuck）等的竞争中崛起。然而，如今的施瓦布，年销售额高达数亿美元。而勒斯·施瓦布本人已是八旬高龄，没受过什么教育，却凭一己之力做成了这一切。

How did he do it? I don’t see a whole lot of people looking like a light bulb357Light bulb灯泡 has come on. Well, let’s think about it with some microeconomic fluency.

他是怎么做到的？我没看到多少人脸上亮起“恍然大悟”的灯泡357Light bulb灯泡。好，让我们用一点微观经济学的流畅思维来想想。

Is there some wave that Schwab could have caught? The minute you ask the question, the answer pops in. The Japanese had a zero position in tires, and they got big. So this guy must have ridden that wave some in the early times. Then, the slow following success has to have some other causes. And what probably happened here, obviously, is this guy did one hell of a lot of things right. And among the things that he must have done right is he must have harnessed what Mankiw calls the superpower of incentives. He must have a very clever incentive structure driving his people. And a clever personnel selection system, etc. And he must be pretty good at advertising. Which he is. He’s an artist.

施瓦布有没有赶上什么浪潮？你一问这问题，答案就冒出来了。日本人在轮胎领域本毫无地位，后来却做大了。所以这人早期必定多少乘上了那股浪潮。接着，随后缓慢的成功必有别的原因。而这里很可能发生的是，这家伙把一大堆事情都做对了。在他必定做对的事情中，必定有一样是运用了曼昆所说的激励的超级力量。他必定有一套非常巧妙的激励机制来驱动员工。还有巧妙的人员选拔系统等。他必定相当擅长广告。他确实擅长。他是个艺术家。

So he had to get a wave in the Japanese tire invasion, the Japanese being as successful as they were. And then a talented fanatic had to get a hell of a lot of things right and keep them right with clever systems. Again, not that hard of an answer. But what else would be a likely cause of the peculiar success?

所以，他必定乘上了日本轮胎入侵的浪潮，日本人确实那么成功。然后，一个天才的狂热者必须把一大堆事情做对，并用巧妙的制度保持正确。同样，答案并不算难。但还有什么可能是这奇特成功的原因呢？

We hire business school graduates, and they’re no better at these problems than you were. Maybe that’s the reason we hire so few of them.

我们聘用商学院毕业生，而他们解决这些问题的能力并不比你们强。也许这正是我们很少聘用他们的原因。

我们聘用商学院毕业生，而他们解决这些问题的能力并不比你们强。也许这正是我们很少聘用他们的原因。

“We hire business school graduates, and they’re no better at these problems than you were. Maybe that’s the reason we hire so few of them.”我们也雇商学院毕业生，而他们处理这些问题并不比你们强。也许正因如此，我们才雇得这么少。

Well, how did I solve those problems? Obviously, I was using a simple search engine in my mind to go through checklist-style, and I was using some rough algorithms that work pretty well in a great many complex systems, and those algorithms run something like this:

好，我是怎么解决这些问题的？显然，我在脑中用一台简单的搜索引擎，像清单那样逐一过筛，用的是一些在大量复杂系统中相当管用的粗略算法，这些算法大致如下：

01Extreme maximization or minimization of one or two variables. Example, Costco or our furniture and appliance store.
02Adding success factors so that a bigger combination drives success, often in nonlinear fashion, as one is reminded by the concept of breakpoint and the concept of critical mass in physics. Often, results are not linear. You get a little bit more mass and you get a lollapalooza result. And, of course, I’ve been searching for lollapalooza results all my life, so I’m very interested in models that explain their occurrence.
03An extreme of good performance over many factors. Example, Toyota or Les Schwab.
04Catching and riding some sort of big wave. Example, Oracle. By the way, I cited Oracle before I knew that the Oracle CFO [Jeff Henley] was a big part of the proceedings here today.

Generally, I recommend and use in problem-solving cut-to-the-quick algorithms, and I find you have to use them both forward and backward. Let me give you an example. I irritate my family by giving them little puzzles, and one of the puzzles that I gave my family not very long ago was when I said, “There’s an activity in America with one-on-one contests and a national championship. The same person won the championship on two occasions about 65 years apart. Now,” I said, “name the activity.”

总的来说，我推荐并在解决问题时使用快刀斩乱麻式的算法，而且我发现你必须正着、反着都用它们。

总的来说，我推荐并在解决问题时使用快刀斩乱麻式的算法，而且我发现你必须正着、反着都用它们。

让我给你们举个例子。我常出些小谜题惹我的家人烦，不久前我给家人出的一个谜题是：“美国有一项运动，是一对一的较量，还有全国冠军赛。同一个人两次夺得冠军，中间相隔约65年。现在，”我说，“说出这项运动的名字。”

“Generally, I recommend and use in problem-solving cut-to-the-quick algorithms, and I find you have to use them both forward and backward.”通常，我推荐并在解题时使用直击要害的算法，而且我发现，你得正反两个方向都用。

Again, I don’t see a lot of light bulbs going on. And in my family, not a lot of light bulbs were flashing. But I have a physicist son who has been trained more in the type of thinking I like. And he immediately got the right answer, and here’s the way he reasoned: It can’t be anything requiring a lot of hand-eye coordination. Nobody 85 years of age is going to win a national billiards tournament, much less a national tennis tournament. It just can’t be. Then he figured it couldn’t be chess, which this physicist plays very well, because it’s too hard. The complexity of the system and the stamina required are too great. But that led into checkers.361Checkers西洋跳棋 And he thought, “Aha! There’s a game where vast experience might guide you to be the best even though you’re 85 years of age.”

再说一遍，我没看到多少灯泡亮起。我家里人也没几盏灯泡在闪。但我有个当物理学家的儿子，受的训练更接近我喜欢的那种思维。他立刻给出了正确答案，推理如下：它不可能是任何需要大量手眼协调的运动。85岁的人绝不可能赢得全国台球锦标赛，更别提全国网球锦标赛了。绝不可能。接着他推断不可能是国际象棋——这位物理学家棋下得很好——因为太难了。系统的复杂性和所需耐力都太大。但这把他引向了西洋跳棋。361Checkers西洋跳棋他想：“啊哈！有一种游戏，即便你85岁，丰富经验也能指引你成为最强者。”

Anyway, I recommend that sort of mental puzzle-solving to all of you, flipping one’s thinking both backward and forward. And I recommend that academic economics get better at very small-scale microeconomics as demonstrated here.

总之，我向你们所有人推荐那种心智解谜，把思维正反来回翻转。我也建议学院派经济学在如这里所示的小规模微观经济学上做得更好。

FiveToo little synthesis in economics

My fifth criticism is there is too little synthesis in economics, not only with matter outside traditional economics but also within economics.

我的第五条批评是，经济学中的综合太少了，不仅与传统经济学之外的事物缺乏综合，经济学内部也缺乏综合。

I have posed before two different business school classes the following problem. I say, “You have studied supply and demand curves. You have learned that when you raise the price, ordinarily the volume you can sell goes down, and when you reduce the price, the volume you can sell goes up. Is that right? That’s what you’ve learned?” They all nod yes. And I say, “Now tell me several instances when, if you want the physical volume to go up, the correct answer is to increase the price.” And there’s this long and ghastly pause. And finally, in each of the two business schools in which I’ve tried this, maybe one person in 50 could name one instance. They come up with the idea that under certain circumstances, a higher price acts as a rough indicator of quality and thereby increases sales volumes.362Beckman Instruments贝克曼仪器公司

我以前给两个不同的商学院班级出过下面这个问题。我说：“你们学过供给与需求曲线。你们学到，提价时通常销量下降，降价时销量上升。对不对？你们学的是这个？”他们都点头说是。然后我说：“现在告诉我几个例子，说明如果你想让实物销量上升，正确的做法是提价。”于是出现了漫长而可怕的沉默。最终，在我试过的这两所商学院里，50个人里大概只有1个能举出一个例子。他们想到的是：在某些情况下，高价作为质量的粗略指标，反而会提高销量。

This happened in the case of my friend Bill Ballhaus. When he was head of Beckman Instruments, it produced some complicated product where if it failed, it caused enormous damage to the purchaser. It wasn’t a pump at the bottom of an oil well, but that’s a good mental example. And he realized that the reason this thing was selling so poorly, even though it was better than anybody else’s product, was because it was priced lower. It made people think it was a low-quality gizmo. So he raised the price by 20 percent or so, and the volume went way up.

我朋友比尔·鲍尔豪斯（Bill Ballhaus）就遇到过这种情况。他执掌贝克曼仪器公司362Beckman Instruments贝克曼仪器公司（Beckman Instruments）时，公司生产一种复杂产品，一旦失效会给购买者造成巨大损失。它不是油井底的泵，但那是个很好的思维例子。他意识到，这东西卖得这么差，尽管比任何竞品都好，原因就在于定价太低。这让人以为它是低质小玩意。于是他把价格提高约20%，销量就大幅上去了。

But only one in 50 can come up with this sole instance in a modern business school—one of the business schools being Stanford, which is hard to get into. And nobody has yet come up with the main answer that I like. Suppose you raise that price and use the extra money to bribe the other guy’s purchasing agent? Is that going to work? And are there functional equivalents in economics, microeconomics, of raising the price and using the extra sales proceeds to drive sales higher? And, of course, there are a zillion, once you’ve made that mental jump. It’s so simple.

但在现代商学院里，50人中只有1个能想到这唯一的例子——其中一所还是很难考进的斯坦福。而至今没人给出我最喜欢的主要答案。假设你在提价后，用多出来的钱去贿赂对方的采购代理？这行得通吗？在经济学、微观经济学中，有没有与“提价并用额外销售收入推动更高销量”功能等同的做法？当然有成千上万种，只要你完成那一下思维跳跃。就是这么简单。

One of the most extreme examples is in the investment management field. Suppose you’re the manager of a mutual fund, and you want to sell more. People commonly come to the following answer: You raise the commissions, which, of course, reduces the number of units of real investments delivered to the ultimate buyer, so you’re increasing the price per unit of real investment that you’re selling the ultimate customer. And you’re using that extra commission to bribe the customer’s purchasing agent. You’re bribing the broker to betray his client and put the client’s money into the high-commission product. This has worked to produce at least a trillion dollars of mutual fund sales.363John Maynard Keynes约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯

最极端的例子之一在投资管理领域。假设你是某共同基金经理，想卖更多。人们通常会得出如下答案：你提高佣金，这当然减少了交付给最终买家的真实投资单位数，所以你是在提高卖给最终客户的每单位真实投资的价格。而你用那笔额外佣金去贿赂客户的采购代理。你贿赂经纪人，让他背叛客户，把客户的钱投进高佣金产品。这一招已制造出至少一万亿美元的共同基金销售额。

This tactic is not an attractive part of human nature, and I want to tell you that I pretty completely avoided it in my life. I don’t think it’s necessary to spend your life selling what you would never buy. Even though it’s legal, I don’t think it’s a good idea. But you shouldn’t accept all my notions, because you’ll risk becoming unemployable. You shouldn’t take my notions unless you’re willing to risk being unemployable by all but a few.

这种策略并非人性中可爱的一面，而我想告诉你们，我一生几乎完全避开了它。我认为没必要终其一生去卖你自己绝不会买的东西。即便它合法，我也不认为这是个好主意。但你们不应全盘接受我的观念，否则会有变得找不到工作的风险。除非你们愿意承担“除少数地方外无人雇用”的风险，否则别接受我的观念。

除非你们愿意承担“除少数地方外无人雇用”的风险，否则别接受我的观念。

“You shouldn’t take my notions unless you’re willing to risk being unemployable by all but a few.”除非你甘愿冒『除极少数人外无人雇你』的风险，否则不该采纳我的那些观念。

I think my experience with my simple question is an example of how little synthesis people get, even in advanced academic settings, considering economic questions. Obvious questions, with such obvious answers. Yet people take four courses in economics, go to business school, have all these IQ points, and write all these essays, but they can’t synthesize worth a damn.

我认为我用这个简单问题得到的经验，正说明即便在高级学术环境里，人们在思考经济问题时综合得有多么少。明显的问题，有着明显的答案。然而人们修过四门经济学课，念了商学院，有那么多智商点数，写了那么多论文，却毫无综合的能力。

This failure is not because the professors know all this stuff and they’re deliberately withholding it from the students. This failure happens because the professors aren’t all that good at this kind of synthesis. They were trained in a different way. I can’t remember if it was Keynes or Galbraith364John Kenneth GalbraithJohn Kenneth Galbraith (1908–2006) , born in Ontario, Canada, graduated from Ontario Agricultural College and went on for a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley. In 1949, he joined the economics faculty at Harvard University. A friend of President John F. Kennedy, Galbraith served as US ambassador to India from 1961 to 1963. As an economist, Galbraith held progressive values and wrote accessible books that often describe how economic theory does not always mesh with real life. Among his best-known works are American Capitalism: The Concept of Countervailing Power (1952), The Affluent Society (1958), and The New Industrial State (1967).约翰·肯尼斯·加尔布雷思（John Kenneth Galbraith，1908–2006 年）生于加拿大安大略，毕业于安大略农学院，后从加州大学伯克利分校获得博士学位。1949 年，他加入哈佛大学经济学教师队伍。作为肯尼迪总统的朋友，加尔布雷思 1961 年至 1963 年出任美国驻印度大使。作为经济学家，加尔布雷思秉持进步价值观，写的书通俗易懂，常常描述经济理论并不总能与现实生活吻合。他的名著包括《美国资本主义：抗衡力量的概念》（American Capitalism: The Concept of Countervailing Power，1952）、《丰裕社会》（The Affluent Society，1958）和《新工业国》（The New Industrial State，1967）。 who said that economics professors are most economical with ideas. They make a few they learned in graduate school last a lifetime.

这种失败，不是因为教授们知道这一切却故意对学生藏着掖着。这种失败之所以发生，是因为教授们本身就不太擅长这种综合。他们受的是另一种训练。我记不清是凯恩斯341John Maynard KeynesJohn Maynard Keynes (1883–1946) , son of an economics lecturer at Cambridge University and a social reformist, seemed destined to become a great economist and political thinker. His book, The General Theory of Employment, Interest, and Money , published in 1936, advocated that government stimulate demand in times of high unemployment—for example, by spending on public works. The book serves as the foundation of modern macroeconomics.约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯（John Maynard Keynes，1883–1946 年）是剑桥大学一位经济学讲师和社会改革论者之子，似乎注定要成为伟大的经济学家和政治思想家。他 1936 年出版的著作《就业、利息和货币通论》（The General Theory of Employment, Interest, and Money）主张，在高失业时期政府应刺激需求，例如通过公共工程支出。该书是现代宏观经济学的基石。还是加尔布雷斯（Galbraith）说过，经济学教授在思想上最“节约”。他们把研究生院学到的一点东西，用上一辈子。

The second interesting problem with synthesis involves two of the most famous examples in economics. Number one is [David] Ricardo’s365David RicardoDavid Ricardo (1772–1823) , born in London, began working with his father at the London Stock Exchange at age 14. His wealth allowed him to retire young, and he secured a seat in Parliament. He became interested in economics after reading Adam Smith’s The Wealth of Nations and made many significant contributions to the field. Ricardo is often credited with the theory of comparative advantage, which explains why it can be beneficial for two countries to trade even though one of them may be able to produce every kind of item more cheaply than the other. The concept was first described by Robert Torrens in 1815 in an essay on the wheat trade, but Ricardo explained it more clearly in his 1817 book The Principles of Political Economy and Taxation.大卫·李嘉图（David Ricardo，1772–1823 年）生于伦敦，14 岁开始在伦敦证券交易所与父亲共事。他的财富让他得以早早退休，并获得了一个议会席位。读了亚当·斯密的《国富论》后，他对经济学产生了兴趣，并为该领域作出许多重大贡献。李嘉图常被认为提出了比较优势理论，它解释了为什么即使一国能够比另一国更便宜地生产每一种商品，两国之间贸易仍然可能对彼此有利。这一概念最早由罗伯特·托伦斯（Robert Torrens）在 1815 年一篇关于小麦贸易的文章中描述，但李嘉图在 1817 年的著作《政治经济学及赋税原理》（The Principles of Political Economy and Taxation）中阐释得更清楚。 principle of comparative advantage376 in trade, and the other is Adam Smith’s pin factory. And both of these, of course, work to vastly increase economic output per person, and they’re similar in that each somehow directs functions into the hands of people who are very good at doing the functions. Yet they’re radically different examples in that one of them is the ultimate example of central planning—the pin factory—where the whole system was planned by somebody, while the other example, Ricardo’s, happens automatically as a natural consequence of trade.

第二个与综合有关的趣题，涉及经济学中最著名的两个例子。其一是李嘉图365David RicardoDavid Ricardo (1772–1823) , born in London, began working with his father at the London Stock Exchange at age 14. His wealth allowed him to retire young, and he secured a seat in Parliament. He became interested in economics after reading Adam Smith’s The Wealth of Nations and made many significant contributions to the field. Ricardo is often credited with the theory of comparative advantage, which explains why it can be beneficial for two countries to trade even though one of them may be able to produce every kind of item more cheaply than the other. The concept was first described by Robert Torrens in 1815 in an essay on the wheat trade, but Ricardo explained it more clearly in his 1817 book The Principles of Political Economy and Taxation.大卫·李嘉图（David Ricardo，1772–1823 年）生于伦敦，14 岁开始在伦敦证券交易所与父亲共事。他的财富让他得以早早退休，并获得了一个议会席位。读了亚当·斯密的《国富论》后，他对经济学产生了兴趣，并为该领域作出许多重大贡献。李嘉图常被认为提出了比较优势理论，它解释了为什么即使一国能够比另一国更便宜地生产每一种商品，两国之间贸易仍然可能对彼此有利。这一概念最早由罗伯特·托伦斯（Robert Torrens）在 1815 年一篇关于小麦贸易的文章中描述，但李嘉图在 1817 年的著作《政治经济学及赋税原理》（The Principles of Political Economy and Taxation）中阐释得更清楚。（Ricardo）的贸易比较优势原理，其二是亚当·斯密的针厂。两者当然都能极大地提高人均经济产出，相似之处在于，它们都以某种方式把职能交到极擅长该职能的人手中。但它们又截然不同：其中一个——针厂——是中央计划的终极范例，整个系统由某人规划；而另一个，李嘉图的例子，则作为贸易的自然结果自动发生。
