—
George Shultz乔治·舒尔茨

And, of course, once you get into the joys of synthesis, you immediately think, “Do these things interact?” Of course they interact. Beautifully. And that’s one of the causes of the power of a modern economic system.

当然，一旦你体会到综合的乐趣，就会立刻想：“这些事物会相互作用吗？”它们当然会。美妙地相互作用。而这正是现代经济体系威力的一大成因。

I saw an example of that kind of interaction years ago. Berkshire had this former savings and loan company, and it had made this loan on a hotel right opposite the Hollywood Park Racetrack. In due time, the neighborhood changed, and it was full of gangs, pimps, and dope dealers. They tore copper pipe out of the wall for dope fixes, and there were people hanging around the hotel with guns, and nobody would come. We foreclosed on it two or three times, and the loan value went down to nothing. We seemed to have an insolvable economic problem—a microeconomic problem.

多年前我就见过这种相互作用的例子。伯克希尔曾有一家储蓄贷款公司，它给一家正对好莱坞公园赛马场（Hollywood Park Racetrack）的酒店放了贷。时过境迁，街区变了，到处是帮派、皮条客和毒贩。他们为了搞钱买毒，把墙里的铜管拆走，有人带着枪在酒店周围游荡，没人愿意来。我们两三次取消了其赎回权，贷款余额归零。我们似乎遇到了一个无解的经济问题——一个微观经济学问题。

Now, we could have gone to McKinsey, or maybe to a bunch of professors from Harvard, and we would have gotten a report about 10 inches thick about the ways we could approach this failing hotel in this terrible neighborhood. But instead, we put a sign on the property that said, “For sale or rent.” And in came, in response to that sign, a man who said, “I’ll spend $200,000 fixing up your hotel and buy it at a high price on credit if you can get zoning so I can turn the parking lot into a putting green.”

现在，我们本可以去找麦肯锡，或者找一群哈佛教授，会得到一份约10英寸厚的报告，讲我们如何处置这家位于糟糕街区的失败酒店。但我们没有，而是在物业上立了块“出售或出租”的牌子。结果，有个人看到牌子找上门来，说：“如果你能搞定分区规划许可，让我把停车场改成高尔夫推杆练习场，我就花20万美元整修你的酒店，并高价赊账买下它。”

“You’ve got to have a parking lot in a hotel,” we said. “What do you have in mind?”

“酒店总得有停车场啊，”我们说，“你是怎么打算的？”

He said, “No, my business is flying seniors in from Florida, putting them near the airport, and then letting them go out to Disneyland and various places by bus and coming back. I don’t care how bad the neighborhood is going to be because my people are self-contained behind walls. All they have to do is get on the bus in the morning and come home in the evening. They don’t need a parking lot; they need a putting green.”

他说：“不，我的生意是把老年人从佛罗里达（Florida）用飞机接来，安置在机场附近，然后让他们乘大巴去迪士尼乐园（Disneyland）和其他地方，再回来。我不在乎周边街区会多糟，因为我的人被围墙圈在里面，自给自足。他们只需早上上车、晚上回家。他们不需要停车场；他们需要的是推杆练习场。”

So we made the deal with the guy. The whole thing worked beautifully, and the loan got paid off, and it all worked out.

于是我们和那人达成了交易。整件事漂亮地解决了，贷款得以偿还，一切圆满。

Obviously, that’s an interaction of Ricardo and the pin factory examples. The odd system that this guy had designed to amuse seniors was pure pin factory, and finding the guy with this system was pure Ricardo. So these things are interacting.

显然，那是李嘉图与针厂例子的相互作用。那人设计了用来取悦老年人的古怪系统，纯属针厂式；而找到拥有这系统的人，纯属李嘉图式。所以这些事物在相互作用。

那人设计了用来取悦老年人的古怪系统，纯属针厂式；而找到拥有这系统的人，纯属李嘉图式。

“The odd system that this guy had designed to amuse seniors was pure pin factory, and finding the guy with this system was pure Ricardo.”这家伙为逗乐老人而设计的古怪系统，纯然是『别针工厂』（pin factory）；而发现这个系统设计者，纯然是李嘉图（Ricardo）式的。

Well, I’ve taken you partway through the synthesis. It gets harder when you want to figure out how much activity should be within private firms, and how much should be within the government, and what are the factors that determine which functions are where, and why do the failures occur, and so on and so on.

好，我把你们带到了综合的中途。当你想弄清楚多少活动该在企业内部、多少该在政府内部，哪些因素决定了职能的归属，以及失败为何发生时，事情就变得更难了。

It’s my opinion that anybody with a high IQ who graduated in economics ought to be able to sit down and write a 10-page synthesis of all these ideas that’s quite persuasive. And I would bet a lot of money that I could give this test in practically every economics department in the country and get a perfectly lousy bunch of synthesis. They’d give me Ronald Coase.367Ronald CoaseRonald Coase (1910–2013) , born in a suburb of London, graduated from secondary school at age 12 and enrolled in the University of London only two years later. He earned degrees in law and economics and began research into transaction costs. He came to the United States in 1951 for an academic career that started at the University of Buffalo. He settled into the University of Chicago in 1964 and remains there as professor emeritus. His work “The Nature of the Firm” (1937) was cited as a major consideration in his receipt of the Nobel Prize in Economics in 1991.罗纳德·科斯（Ronald Coase，1910–2013 年）生于伦敦郊区，12 岁从中学毕业，仅两年后就进入伦敦大学。他获得法律和经济学学位，并开始研究交易成本。1951 年他来到美国，开启了从布法罗大学起步的学术生涯。1964 年他在芝加哥大学安定下来，至今仍是该校的荣休教授。他的文章《企业的性质》（“The Nature of the Firm”，1937 年）被视为他 1991 年获得诺贝尔经济学奖的主要考量之一。 They’d talk about transaction costs. They’d click off a little something that their professors gave them and spit it back. But in terms of really understanding how it all fits together, I would confidently predict that most people couldn’t do it very well.

我认为，任何高智商的经济学毕业生都应当能坐下来，写一份颇具说服力的、综合所有这些思想的10页文章。我愿赌一大笔钱：如果我在全国几乎每个经济系都出这道考题，得到的综合文章会是一团糟。他们会搬出罗纳德·科斯367Ronald CoaseRonald Coase (1910–2013) , born in a suburb of London, graduated from secondary school at age 12 and enrolled in the University of London only two years later. He earned degrees in law and economics and began research into transaction costs. He came to the United States in 1951 for an academic career that started at the University of Buffalo. He settled into the University of Chicago in 1964 and remains there as professor emeritus. His work “The Nature of the Firm” (1937) was cited as a major consideration in his receipt of the Nobel Prize in Economics in 1991.罗纳德·科斯（Ronald Coase，1910–2013 年）生于伦敦郊区，12 岁从中学毕业，仅两年后就进入伦敦大学。他获得法律和经济学学位，并开始研究交易成本。1951 年他来到美国，开启了从布法罗大学起步的学术生涯。1964 年他在芝加哥大学安定下来，至今仍是该校的荣休教授。他的文章《企业的性质》（“The Nature of the Firm”，1937 年）被视为他 1991 年获得诺贝尔经济学奖的主要考量之一。（Ronald Coase）。他们会谈交易成本。他们会把教授给的一丁点东西机械复述出来。但就真正理解一切如何契合而言，我自信地预言，大多数人做得不会太好。

By the way, if any of you want to try and do this, go ahead. I think you’ll find it hard. In this connection, one of the interesting things that I want to mention is that Max Planck,368Max PlanckBorn in Germany to a law professor father, Max Planck (1858–1947) earned his doctorate at age 21. His earliest work on thermodynamics evolved into an interest in radiation. From these studies, he was led to work on the distribution of energy in the spectrum of radiation. Planck’s work on energy emissions was essential to the field of physics and came to be known as quantum theory. He was awarded the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1918.马克斯·普朗克（Max Planck，1858–1947 年）生于德国，父亲是法学教授，21 岁就获得博士学位。他最早关于热力学的研究，渐渐引向对辐射的兴趣。从这些研究出发，他投入到辐射谱中能量分布的工作。普朗克关于能量发射的工作对物理学领域至关重要，后来被称为量子理论。1918 年，他被授予诺贝尔物理学奖。 the great Nobel laureate who found Planck’s constant, tried once to do economics. He gave it up.

顺便一提，如果你们有人想试试，尽管去。我想你们会发现这很难。与此相关，我想提到一件有趣的事：发现普朗克常数（Planck's constant）的伟大诺贝尔奖得主马克斯·普朗克368Max PlanckBorn in Germany to a law professor father, Max Planck (1858–1947) earned his doctorate at age 21. His earliest work on thermodynamics evolved into an interest in radiation. From these studies, he was led to work on the distribution of energy in the spectrum of radiation. Planck’s work on energy emissions was essential to the field of physics and came to be known as quantum theory. He was awarded the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1918.马克斯·普朗克（Max Planck，1858–1947 年）生于德国，父亲是法学教授，21 岁就获得博士学位。他最早关于热力学的研究，渐渐引向对辐射的兴趣。从这些研究出发，他投入到辐射谱中能量分布的工作。普朗克关于能量发射的工作对物理学领域至关重要，后来被称为量子理论。1918 年，他被授予诺贝尔物理学奖。（Max Planck），曾经试过做经济学。他放弃了。

Now, why did Max Planck, one of the smartest people who ever lived, give up economics? The answer is, he said, “It’s too hard. The best solution you can get is messy and uncertain.” It didn’t satisfy Planck’s craving for order, and so he gave it up. And if Max Planck early on realized he was never going to get perfect order, I will confidently predict that all of the rest of you are going to have exactly the same result.

那么，史上最聪明的人之一马克斯·普朗克，为何放弃了经济学？答案是，他说：“太难了。你能得到的最佳解也是混乱而不确定的。”这满足不了普朗克对秩序的渴望，于是他放弃了。而如果马克斯·普朗克早就意识到自己永远得不到完美的秩序，我自信地预言，你们其余所有人也会得到完全相同的结果。

By the way, there’s a famous story about Max Planck that is apocryphal: After he won his prize, he was invited to lecture everywhere, and he had this chauffeur who drove him around to give public lectures all through Germany. And the chauffeur memorized the lecture, so one day he said, “Gee, Professor Planck, why don’t you let me try it by switching places?” So he got up and gave the lecture. At the end of it, some physicist stood up and posed a question of extreme difficulty. But the chauffeur was up to it. “Well,” he said, “I’m surprised that a citizen of an advanced city like Munich is asking so elementary a question, so I’m going to ask my chauffeur to respond.”

顺便一提，有个关于马克斯·普朗克的著名故事是杜撰的：他获奖后，到处受邀演讲，有个司机开车载他跑遍德国做公开演讲。司机把演讲背了下来，于是有一天他说：“哎呀，普朗克教授，你何不让我换个位置试试？”于是他上台发表了演讲。结束时，某位物理学家站起来提了个极难的问题。但司机应付得来。“嗯，”他说，“慕尼黑（Munich）这样发达城市的市民竟问出如此基础的问题，令我惊讶，所以我要请我的司机来回答。”

SixExtreme and counterproductive psychological ignorance

All right, I’m down to the sixth main defect, and this is a subdivision of the lack of adequate multidisciplinarity: extreme and counterproductive psychological ignorance in economics. Here, I want to give you a very simple problem. I specialize in simple problems.

好，我讲到了第六个主要缺陷，它是“缺乏足够的跨学科性”的一个分支：经济学中对心理学的极度无知，且适得其反。这里，我想给你们一个很简单的问题。我专攻简单问题。

You own a small casino in Las Vegas. It has 50 standard slot machines.369Slot machines老虎机 Identical in appearance, they’re identical in the function. They have exactly the same payout ratios. The things that cause the payouts are exactly the same. They occur in the same percentages. But there’s one machine in this group of slot machines that, no matter where you put it among the 50, in fairly short order, when you go to the machines at the end of the day, there will be 25 percent more winnings from this one machine than from any other machine.

你在拉斯维加斯（Las Vegas）开了家小赌场。它有50台标准老虎机。369Slot machines老虎机外观相同，功能相同。返奖比率完全相同。导致返奖的因素完全相同。它们以相同比例出现。但这组老虎机中有一台，无论你把它摆在50台中的哪个位置，相当短的时间内，当你一天结束时去清点，这台机器的赢钱会比任何其他机器多25%。

Now, surely, I’m not going to have a failure here. What is different about that heavy-winning machine? Can anybody do it?

现在，我在这里肯定不会让你们卡住。那台常赢的机器有何不同？有人能答吗？

Audience member: More people play it.

听众：玩的人更多。

No, no, I want to know why more people play it. What’s different about that machine is people have used modern electronics to give a higher ratio of near misses. That machine is going bar, bar, lemon, bar, bar, grapefruit, way more often than normal machines, and that will cause heavier play.

不，不，我想知道的是为什么更多人去玩它。那台机器的不同之处在于，人们用现代电子技术提高了“差一点就中”的比例。那台机器出现“bar、bar、柠檬、bar、bar、葡萄柚”的频率，远高于普通机器，而这会引发更重的投注。

How do you get an answer like that? Easy. Obviously, there’s a psychological cause: That machine is doing something to trigger some basic psychological response. If you know the psychological factors, if you’ve got them on a checklist in your head, you just run down the factors, and boom! You get to one that must explain this occurrence. There isn’t any other way to do it effectively.

你怎么得到这样的答案？简单。显然，有个心理学上的原因：那台机器在触发某种基本的心理反应。如果你懂那些心理因素，如果在脑中有一份它们的清单，你只需顺着因素往下过，砰！你就会找到一个必定能解释这一现象的因素。没有别的更有效办法。

如果你懂那些心理因素，如果在脑中有一份它们的清单，你只需顺着因素往下过，砰！你就会找到一个必定能解释这一现象的因素。

fig 370
—
Psychological factors
“If you know the psychological factors, if you’ve got them on a checklist in your head, you just run down the factors, and, boom! You get to one that must explain this occurrence.”只要你懂那些心理因素，把它们列成一张脑中清单，你只需顺着清单往下过，砰！就能找到一个必然能解释这一现象的因素。

These answers are not going to come to people who don’t learn these problem-solving methods. If you want to go through life like a one-legged man in an ass-kicking contest, why, be my guest. But if you want to succeed like a strong man with two legs, you have to pick up these methods, including doing micro- and macroeconomics while knowing psychology.

这些答案不会自动降临到没学过这些解题方法的人头上。如果你想这辈子像个独腿人去参加踢屁股大赛，那请便。但如果你想像双腿健全的壮汉那样成功，就必须掌握这些方法，包括在懂心理学的前提下做微观与宏观经济学。

In this vein, I next want to mention a strange Latin American case of a dysfunctional economy that got fixed. In this little subdivision of Latin America, a culture had arisen wherein everybody stole everything. They embezzled from the company; they stole everything that was loose in the community. And, of course, the economy came practically to a halt. And this thing got fixed.

顺着这个思路，接下来我想提一个奇怪的拉丁美洲案例：一个失灵的经济体被修复了。在拉丁美洲的这个小分支里，兴起一种人人偷一切的文化。他们挪用公司公款；偷走社区里一切没固定住的东西。经济自然近乎停摆。而这事被修复了。

Now, where did I read about this case? I’ll give you a hint. It wasn’t in the annals of economics. I found this case in the annals of psychology. Clever people went down and used a bunch of psychological tricks. And they fixed it.

那么，我在哪里读到这个案例的？给你们个提示。它不在经济学年鉴里。我是在心理学年鉴里发现这个案例的。聪明人下去用了一堆心理学技巧。然后把它修复了。

Well, I think there’s no excuse if you’re an economist, when there are wonderful cases like that of the dysfunctional economy becoming fixed, and these simple tricks that solve so many problems, and you don’t know how to do the fixes and understand the problems. Why be so ignorant about psychology that you don’t even know psychology’s tricks that will fix your own dysfunctional economic systems?

我觉得，如果你是个经济学家，面对那些功能失调的经济体被修复的精彩案例、那些能解决众多问题的简单技巧，却既不知道如何施以修复、也不理解问题所在，那是毫无借口的。你又何必在心理学上无知到这种地步——连能修复你自家功能失调的经济体系的心理学把戏都一无所知？

Here, I want to give you an extreme injunction. This is even tougher than the fundamental organizing ethos of hard science. This has been attributed to Samuel Johnson.372Samuel JohnsonSamuel Johnson (1709–1784) , English author and the leading literary scholar and critic of his time, was celebrated for his brilliant and witty conversation. Johnson’s first work of lasting importance, and the one that permanently established his reputation, was his Dictionary of the English Language (1755).塞缪尔·约翰逊（Samuel Johnson，1709–1784 年），英国作家，是他那个时代最杰出的文学学者和批评家，以机敏睿智的谈吐闻名。约翰逊第一部具有持久重要性、也永久奠定其声誉的著作，是他的《英语词典》（Dictionary of the English Language，1755）。 He said, in substance, that if an academic maintains in place an ignorance that can be easily removed with a little work, the conduct of the academic amounts to treachery. That was his word, “treachery.” You can see why I love this stuff. He says you have a duty if you’re an academic to be as little of a klutz as you can possibly be, and therefore you have got to keep grinding out of your system as much removable ignorance as you can remove.

在此，我想给你们一条极严厉的训令。它甚至比硬科学的基本组织信条还要严苛。这话出自塞缪尔·约翰逊372Samuel JohnsonSamuel Johnson (1709–1784) , English author and the leading literary scholar and critic of his time, was celebrated for his brilliant and witty conversation. Johnson’s first work of lasting importance, and the one that permanently established his reputation, was his Dictionary of the English Language (1755).塞缪尔·约翰逊（Samuel Johnson，1709–1784 年），英国作家，是他那个时代最杰出的文学学者和批评家，以机敏睿智的谈吐闻名。约翰逊第一部具有持久重要性、也永久奠定其声誉的著作，是他的《英语词典》（Dictionary of the English Language，1755）。（Samuel Johnson）。他大意是说：倘若一位学者明知某种无知只需稍加努力便可消除，却听任它留存，那么这位学者的行径便等同于背叛。这是他的原话——“背叛”。你们现在明白我为何钟爱此言了。他说，身为学者，你有责任尽可能别做个笨伯，因此你必须不断从你的认知体系中剔除那些可以剔除的无知。

SevenToo little attention to second- and higher-order effects

On to the next one, the seventh defect: too little attention in economics to second-order and even higher-order effects. This defect is quite understandable because the consequences have consequences, and the consequences of the consequences have consequences, and so on. It gets very complicated. When I was a meteorologist, I found this stuff very irritating, and economics makes meteorology look like a tea party.373Loom织布机

下面谈第七个缺陷：经济学对二级、乃至更高级别的后果关注太少。这个缺陷很可理解，因为结果会产生结果，而结果的结果又会产生结果，如此递进，便极其复杂。我当年做气象员时，就觉得这类事情令人头疼；而经济学让气象学看起来简直像一场茶会般简单。

“结果会产生结果，而结果的结果又会产生结果，如此递进。事情变得极其复杂。

“The consequences have consequences, and the consequences of the consequences have consequences, and so on. It gets very complicated.”后果还会生出后果，而后果之后果又生出后果，如此递推。事情就变得极其复杂。

Extreme economic ignorance was displayed when various experts, including PhD economists, forecast the cost of the original Medicare law. They did simple extrapolations of past costs. Well, the cost forecast was off by a factor of more than 1,000 percent. The cost they projected was less than 10 percent of the cost that happened. Once they put in place various new incentives, the behavior changed in response to the incentives, and the numbers became quite different from their projection. And medicine invented new and expensive remedies, as it was sure to do.

当年多位专家（其中包括拥有博士学位的经济学家）对最初的医疗保险法（Medicare）的成本进行预测时，表现出了极度的经济无知。他们只是把过去的成本简单外推。结果呢，成本预测偏差超过1000%。他们预测的成本还不到实际发生成本的10%。一旦他们设立了各种新的激励，人们的行为便随激励而改变，数字也就与他们的预测大相径庭。而且医学界果然如期发明了昂贵的新疗法。

How could a great group of experts make such a silly forecast? Answer: They oversimplified to get easy figures, like the rube rounding pi to 3.2. They chose not to consider effects of effects of effects, and so on.

一群顶尖专家怎么会做出如此愚蠢的预测？答案是：他们为了得出好算的数字而过度简化，就像乡下佬把圆周率约成3.2一样。他们选择不去考虑后果的后果的后果，如此递推。

One good thing about this common form of misthinking from the viewpoint of academia is that businesspeople are even more foolish about microeconomics. The business version of the Medicare-type insanity is when you own a textile plant and a guy comes in and says, “Oh, isn’t this wonderful? They invented a new loom. It’ll pay for itself in three years at current prices because it adds so much efficiency to the production of textiles.” And you keep buying these looms, and their equivalent, for 20 years, and you keep making 4 percent on capital; you never go anywhere. And the answer is, it wasn’t that the technology didn’t work, it’s that the laws of economics caused the benefit from the new looms to go to the people that bought the textiles, not to the guy who owned the textile plant.

从学术界的眼光看，这种常见的误思有一点好处：生意人在微观经济学上犯的错误更蠢。商界版的“医疗保险式疯狂”是这样的：你拥有一家纺织厂，某人对你说：“哎呀，这难道不妙吗？他们发明了一种新织机。按当前价格，它三年就能收回成本，因为它大大提高了纺织生产效率。”于是你连续二十年不断买这种织机及其同类设备，资本回报率却始终只有4%；你一事无成。答案在于：并非技术不奏效，而是经济规律使然——新织机带来的好处落到了购买纺织品的人手里，而非纺织厂老板的口袋里。

How could anybody not know that if he’d taken freshman economics or been through business school? I think the schools are doing a lousy job. Otherwise, such insanities wouldn’t happen so often.

一个人只要上过大一经济学或念过商学院，怎么会不懂这个道理？我认为学校教得糟透了。否则，这种蠢事不会如此频繁地发生。

Usually, I don’t use formal projections. I don’t let people do them for me because I don’t like throwing up on the desk, but I see them made in a very foolish way all the time, and many people believe in them, no matter how foolish they are. It’s an effective sales technique in America to put a foolish projection on a desk. And if you’re an investment banker, it’s an art form. I don’t read their projections either. Once, Warren and I bought a company, and the seller had a big study done by an investment banker. It was about this thick. We just turned it over as if it were a diseased carcass. He said, “We paid $2 million for that.” I said, “We don’t use them. Never look at them.”

通常我不使用正式的可行性预测。我也不让别人替我做，因为我不喜欢往办公桌上吐。但我总看到有人以极其愚蠢的方式做这些预测，而且许多人深信不疑，无论它们多蠢。在美国，把一份愚蠢的预测丢在桌上是一种有效的推销技巧。若你是投资银行家，那更是一门艺术。我也从不看他们的预测。有一次沃伦（Warren Buffett）和我收购一家公司，卖方请投资银行家做了份厚厚的研究报告。差不多这么厚。我们直接把它像处理一具病尸般翻到一边。他说：“我们为那份报告花了200万美元。”我说：“我们不用那玩意儿。从来不看。”

Anyway, as the Medicare example showed, all human systems are gamed, for reasons rooted deeply in psychology, and great skill is displayed in the gaming because game theory has so much potential. That’s what’s wrong with the workers’ comp system in California. Gaming has been raised to an art form. In the course of gaming the system, people learn to be crooked. Is this good for civilization? Is it good for economic performance? Hell no. The people who design easily gameable systems belong in the lowest circle of Hell.

无论如何，正如医疗保险的例子所示，所有人类制度都会被钻空子，其根源深植于心理学；而人们在博弈中展现出高超的技巧，因为博弈论潜力无穷。加利福尼亚州（California）的工伤赔偿制度正是病根所在。钻空子在此已被提升到一门艺术。在钻制度漏洞的过程中，人们学会了奸诈。这对文明有益吗？对经济表现有益吗？见鬼，当然没有。那些设计出容易被钻空子的制度的人，该被打入地狱的最底层。

“那些设计出容易被钻空子的制度的人，该被打入地狱的最底层。

“The people who design easily gameable systems belong in the lowest circle of Hell.”那些设计出容易被钻空子的系统的人，应下地狱的最底层。

I’ve got a friend whose family controls about 8 percent of the truck trailer market. He just closed his last factory in California, and he had one in Texas that was even worse. The workers’ comp cost in his Texas plant got to be double-digit percentages of payroll. Well, there’s no such profit in making truck trailers. He closed his plant and moved it to Ogden, Utah, where a bunch of believing Mormons are raising big families and don’t game the workers’ comp system. The workers’ comp expense is 2 percent of payroll.

我有个朋友，他的家族控制了约8%的货柜拖车市场。他刚关掉了在加州（California）的最后一家工厂，而在得克萨斯州（Texas）还有一家，情况更糟。他得州工厂的工伤赔偿成本占薪酬支出已高达两位数百分比。可制造货柜拖车本就没有这等利润。他关掉工厂，迁往犹他州（Utah）的奥格登市（Ogden），那里有一群笃信摩门教（Mormon）的人，养育着大家庭，从不钻工伤赔偿制度的空子。其工伤赔偿支出仅占薪酬的2%。

Are the Latinos who were peopling his plant in Texas intrinsically dishonest or bad compared to the Mormons? No. It’s just the incentive structure that so rewards all this fraud is put in place by these ignorant legislatures, many members of which have been to law school, and they just don’t think about what terrible things they’re doing to the civilization because they don’t take into account the second-order effects and the third-order effects in lying and cheating. So this happens everywhere, and when economics is full of it, it is just like the rest of life.

在他得州工厂里干活的那些拉美人，比起摩门教徒，天生就不诚实、不道德的吗？不是。症结只在于激励结构——这种结构如此奖赏欺诈，而它正是由那些无知的立法者设立的，其中许多人还念过法学院。他们从不考虑说谎和欺骗造成的二级、三级后果，因此根本不去想自己给文明带来了多大的祸害。所以此类现象随处可见；当经济学充斥着这种事时，它便和生活的其他部分别无二致。

There was a wonderful example of gaming a human system in the career of Victor Niederhoffer375Victor NiederhofferVictor Niederhoffer (b. 1943) studied statistics and economics, earning an undergraduate degree at Harvard and a PhD at the University of Chicago. He taught at the University of California, Berkeley for five years and simultaneously ran Niederhoffer, Cross & Zeckhauser, Inc., involved in selling private firms to public companies. In the late 1970s, Niederhoffer started trading futures and options. He founded a trading firm, Niederhoffer Investments, in 1980 to provide financial management for institutional clients. He is also a past multiyear national squash champion.维克多·尼德霍夫（Victor Niederhoffer，1943 年生）学习统计学和经济学，在哈佛获得本科学位，在芝加哥大学获得博士学位。他在加州大学伯克利分校任教五年，同时经营 Niederhoffer, Cross & Zeckhauser 公司，从事把私人公司卖给上市公司的业务。70 年代末，尼德霍夫开始交易期货和期权。1980 年他创立了交易公司 Niederhoffer Investments，为机构客户提供财务管理。他还曾是多年的全国壁球冠军。 in the economics department of Harvard. Victor Niederhoffer was the son of a police lieutenant, and he needed to get As at Harvard. But he didn’t want to do any serious work at Harvard because what he really liked doing was 1) playing world-class checkers; 2) gambling in high-stakes card games, at which he was very good, all hours of the day and night; 3) being the squash champion of the United States, which he was for years; and 4) being about as good a tennis player as a part-time tennis player could be.

维克多·尼德霍夫375Victor NiederhofferVictor Niederhoffer (b. 1943) studied statistics and economics, earning an undergraduate degree at Harvard and a PhD at the University of Chicago. He taught at the University of California, Berkeley for five years and simultaneously ran Niederhoffer, Cross & Zeckhauser, Inc., involved in selling private firms to public companies. In the late 1970s, Niederhoffer started trading futures and options. He founded a trading firm, Niederhoffer Investments, in 1980 to provide financial management for institutional clients. He is also a past multiyear national squash champion.维克多·尼德霍夫（Victor Niederhoffer，1943 年生）学习统计学和经济学，在哈佛获得本科学位，在芝加哥大学获得博士学位。他在加州大学伯克利分校任教五年，同时经营 Niederhoffer, Cross & Zeckhauser 公司，从事把私人公司卖给上市公司的业务。70 年代末，尼德霍夫开始交易期货和期权。1980 年他创立了交易公司 Niederhoffer Investments，为机构客户提供财务管理。他还曾是多年的全国壁球冠军。（Victor Niederhoffer）在哈佛大学（Harvard）经济学系的经历，是钻人类制度空子的绝佳例子。尼德霍夫是一名警察中尉的儿子，他必须在哈佛拿到甲等成绩。但他不想在哈佛认真做功课，因为他真正爱好的是：一、下世界级的西洋跳棋；二、不分昼夜地玩高额赌注的纸牌，而且玩得极好；三、做美国壁球冠军——他连任多年；四、当一个业余网球手能达到的顶尖高手。

This did not leave much time for getting As at Harvard, so he went into the economics department. You’d think he would have chosen French poetry. But remember, this was a guy who could play championship checkers. He thought he was up to outsmarting the Harvard economics department. And he was.

如此一来，他可用于在哈佛拿甲等的闲暇便所剩无几，于是他选了经济学系。你或许以为他会去读法国诗歌。但别忘了，这家伙可是能下冠军级西洋跳棋的。他自认有本事耍弄哈佛经济学系。而他确实做到了。

He noticed that the graduate students did most of the boring work that would otherwise go to the professors, and he noticed that because it was so hard to get to be a graduate student at Harvard, they were all very brilliant and organized and hardworking, as well as much needed by grateful professors. And therefore, by custom, and as would be predicted from the psychological force called reciprocity tendency, in a really advanced graduate course, the professors always gave an A. So Victor Niederhoffer signed up for nothing but the most advanced graduate courses in the Harvard economics department, and of course he got A after A after A after A, and was hardly ever near a class. And for a while, some people at Harvard may have thought it had a new prodigy on its hands.

他发现研究生承担了绝大部分本应由教授完成的枯燥工作；他又发现，由于进哈佛读研究生极难，这些研究生个个聪慧、有条理、勤奋，又深受教授们倚重与感激。因此，依惯例，也如“互惠倾向”这一心理力量所能预料，在真正高阶的研究生课程里，教授总是给甲等。于是尼德霍夫专挑哈佛经济学系那些最高阶的研究生课程报名，自然是一个甲等接一个甲等，而几乎从不去上课。有段时间，哈佛某些人还以为本校出了个新天才。

That’s a ridiculous story, but the scheme will work still. And Niederhoffer is famous: They call his style “Niederhoffering the curriculum.”

这故事荒唐，但这套办法至今仍然奏效。尼德霍夫由此成名：人们把他这种做派叫做“尼德霍夫选课法”（Niederhoffering the curriculum）。

This shows how all human systems are gamed. Another example of not thinking through the consequences of the consequences is the standard reaction in economics to Ricardo’s law of comparative advantage giving benefit on both sides of trade.

这说明了所有人类制度如何被钻空子。另一个不深究后果的后果的例子，是经济学界对李嘉图（David Ricardo）比较优势定律的标准反应——该定律认为贸易对双方都有利。

Ricardo came up with a wonderful, nonobvious explanation that was so powerful that people were charmed with it, and they still are because it’s a very useful idea. Everybody in economics understands that comparative advantage is a big deal when one considers first-order advantages in trade from the Ricardo effect. But suppose you’ve got a very talented ethnic group, like the Chinese, and they’re very poor, and you’re an advanced nation, and you create free trade with China, and it goes on for a long time. Now let’s follow second- and third-order consequences. You are more prosperous than you would have been if you hadn’t traded with China in terms of average well-being in the United States, right? Ricardo proved it. But which nation is going to be growing faster in economic terms? It’s obviously China. They’re absorbing all the modern technology of the world through this great facilitator in free trade, and, like the Asian Tigers have proved, they will get ahead fast. Look at Hong Kong. Look at Taiwan. Look at early Japan.

李嘉图提出了一个精彩而绝非显而易见的解释，其力量如此之强，以至于人们为之倾倒，至今依然，因为它极有用处。经济学界人人都明白，若只看李嘉图效应带来的初级贸易优势，比较优势便是件大事。

但假设你面对的是一个极具天赋的族群，比如中国人，他们极穷；而你是一个发达国家，与中国建立自由贸易，并长期维持。现在让我们追踪二级和三级后果。就美国平均福祉而言，你比不与中国贸易时更富裕了，对吧？李嘉图证明了这一点。但哪个国家的经济增长会更快？显然是中国。通过自由贸易这一伟大的推动者，他们正吸收全世界的现代技术；正如亚洲四小龙（Asian Tigers）所证明的，他们会迅速赶超。看看香港。看看台湾。看看早年的日本。

So you start in a place where you’ve got a weak nation of a billion and a quarter people, and in the end, they’re going to be a much bigger, stronger nation than you are, maybe even having more and better atomic bombs. Well, Ricardo did not prove that that’s a wonderful outcome for the former leading nation. He didn’t try to determine second-order and higher-order effects.

于是你从这样一个起点出发：一个拥有十二亿多人口的弱国，而到头来，他们会成为比你们庞大、强盛得多的国家，甚至可能拥有更多、更好的原子弹。可是，李嘉图并未证明这对原先的领先国家是个美妙结局。他根本没想去确定二级及更高级别的后果。

If you try to talk like this to economics professors—and I’ve done this three times—they shrink in horror and offense because they don’t like this kind of talk. It really gums up this nice discipline of theirs, which is so much simpler when you ignore second- and third-order consequences.

如果你试着这样跟经济学教授们讲——我试过三次——他们会惊惧而反感地缩回去，因为他们不喜欢这种论调。这确实会把他们那门漂亮的学科搅得一团糟，而只要忽略二级、三级后果，它便简单得多。

The best answer I ever got on that subject—in three tries—was from George Shultz. He said, “Charlie, the way I figure it is if we stop trading with China, the other advanced nations will do it anyway. We wouldn’t stop the ascent of China compared to us, and we’d lose the Ricardo-diagnosed advantages of trade.” Which is obviously correct.

关于这个话题，我在三次尝试中得到的最佳答案，来自乔治·舒尔茨338George Shultz乔治·舒尔茨（George Shultz）。他说：“查理，我是这么想的：就算我们停止和中国贸易，其他发达国家照样会这么做。我们无法遏制中国相对我们的上升势头，而且会丢掉李嘉图所诊断出的贸易优势。”这显然是对的。

I said, “Well, George, you’ve just invented a new form of the tragedy of the commons. You’re locked in this system, and you can’t fix it. You’re going to go to a tragic hell in a handbasket, if going to hell involves being once the great leader of the world and finally going to the shallows in terms of leadership.”

我说：“好吧，乔治，你刚刚发明了一种新形式的公用品悲剧（tragedy of the commons）。你身陷这个体系，却无从修补。若说下地狱意味着曾是世界领袖、最终却在领导地位上退入浅滩，那你正坐着篮筐坠向悲剧的地狱。”

And he said, “Charlie, I do not want to think about this.”

他说：“查理，我不想思考这个问题。”

I think he’s wise. He’s even older than I am, and maybe I should learn from him.

我觉得他很明智。他甚至比我还年长，或许我该向他学学。

EightNot enough attention to the concept of febezzlement

Okay, I’m now down to my eighth objection: too little attention within economics to the simplest and most fundamental principle of algebra.378AlgebraThe word “algebra” is derived from the Arabic word which appears in the treatise The Compendious Book on Calculation by Completion and Balancing, written in 820 by Persian mathematician Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Khwārizmī. The book provides systematic solutions of linear and quadratic equations.“代数”（algebra）一词源自阿拉伯语，见于波斯数学家穆罕默德·伊本·穆萨·花拉子米（Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Khwārizmī）公元 820 年所著的《化简与平衡计算手册》（The Compendious Book on Calculation by Completion and Balancing）。该书给出了一次方程和二次方程的系统解法。

好，我现在说到第八个反对意见：经济学对最简单、最基础的代数原理关注太少。

Now, this sounds outrageous, that economics doesn’t do algebra, right? Well, I want to try an example—I may be wrong on this. I’m old and I’m iconoclastic. But I throw it out anyway. I say that economics doesn’t pay enough attention to the concept of febezzlement. And that I derive from Galbraith’s idea.

这听起来很离谱——经济学居然不运用代数，对吧？好吧，我想举个例子——我这点未必对。我老了，又爱唱反调。但无论如何我还是抛出来。我说，经济学对“捞灰金”（febezzlement）这一概念关注不够。这观点我是从加尔布雷斯（John Kenneth Galbraith）那里引伸来的。

Galbraith’s idea was that if you have an undisclosed embezzlement, it has a wonderful Keynesian stimulating effect on the economy because the guy who’s been embezzled thinks he is as rich as he always was and spends accordingly, and the guy who has stolen the money gets all this new purchasing power. I think that’s correct analysis on Galbraith’s part. The trouble with his notion is that he’s described a minor phenomenon. Because when the embezzlement is discovered, as it almost surely will be, the effect will quickly reverse. So the effect quickly cancels out.

加尔布雷斯的观点是：若存在未败露的贪污，它会对经济产生美妙的凯恩斯式刺激效应——因为被偷的人以为自己仍和从前一样富有，照旧消费，而偷钱的人则获得全新的购买力。我认为加尔布雷斯的分析是对的。他这一观念的麻烦在于，他描述的是一个影响较小的现象。因为贪污一旦败露（几乎必然败露），效应便会迅速逆转。于是效应很快抵消。

But suppose you paid a lot of attention to algebra, which I guess Galbraith didn’t, and you think, “Well, the fundamental principle of algebra is ‘If A is equal to B and B is equal to C, then A is equal to C.’” You’ve then got a fundamental principle that demands that you look for functional equivalents, all you can find.

但假如你（我想加尔布雷斯没有）十分重视代数，你会想：“代数的基本原理是‘若A等于B，B等于C，则A等于C。’”你于是便有了一条基本原理，要求你去寻找功能上的等价物，能找多少找多少。

So suppose you ask the question “Is there such a thing in economics as a febezzlement?” By the way, Galbraith invented the word “bezzle” to describe the amount of undisclosed embezzlement, so I invented the word “febezzlement,” the functional equivalent of embezzlement. This happened after I asked the question “Is there a functional equivalent of embezzlement?” I came up with a lot of wonderful, affirmative answers. Some were in investment management. After all, I’m near investment management. I considered the billions of dollars totally wasted in the course of investing common stock portfolios for American owners. As long as the market keeps going up, the guy who’s wasting all this money doesn’t feel it because he’s looking at these steadily rising values. And to the guy who is getting the money for investment advice, the money looks like well-earned income when he’s really selling detriment for money—surely the functional equivalent of undisclosed embezzlement. You can see why I don’t get invited to many lectures.

于是你问：“经济学中有没有‘捞灰金’这种东西？”顺带一提，加尔布雷斯生造了“bezzle”（黑金）一词，指未败露的贪污数额；所以我生造了“febezzlement”（捞灰金）一词——即贪污的功能等价物。

这发生在我问出“是否存在贪污的功能等价物？”之后。我得到了许多精彩而肯定的答案。有些出现在投资管理业——毕竟我贴近这行。我想到，在为美国股东投资普通股组合的过程中，有数十亿美元被彻底浪费。只要市场持续上涨，浪费这些钱的人便毫无察觉，因为他看到的只是稳步攀升的市值。而对那收取投资建议费的人来说，这笔钱看似正当收入，可他实际上是在拿损害换钱——这无疑是未败露贪污的功能等价物。你们现在明白为何鲜少有人邀我演讲了吧。

So I say, if you look in the economy for febezzlement, the functional equivalent of embezzlement, you’ll find some enormously powerful factors. They create some wealth effect that is on steroids compared to the old wealth effect. But practically nobody thinks as I do, and I quitclaim my idea to any hungry graduate student who has independent means, which he will need before his thesis topic is approved.

所以我说，若你在经济中寻觅“捞灰金”——贪污的功能等价物——你会发现一些极为强大的因素。它们创造的财富效应，比起旧的财富效应，简直是打了兴奋剂。但几乎无人像我这样想，我愿把这一想法的所有权让渡给任何有独立财源、饥渴求知的研究生——而在论文题目获批之前，他正需要这笔财源。

NineNot enough attention to virtue and vice effects

Okay, my ninth objection: not enough attention to virtue and vice379Virtue and vice美德与恶行 effects in economics.

好，我的第九个反对意见：经济学对美德效应与恶行效应关注不足。

It has been plain to me since early life that there are enormous virtue effects in economics and also enormous vice effects. But economists get very uncomfortable when you talk about virtue and vice. It doesn’t lend itself to a lot of columns of numbers. But I would argue that there are big virtue effects in economics. I would say that the spreading of double-entry bookkeeping by the monk Fra Luca de Pacioli380Fra Luca de PacioliFra Luca de Pacioli (1445–1517) in 1494 published his seminal work, The Collected Knowledge of Arithmetic, Geometry, Proportion, and Proportionality. In one section of the book, Pacioli described a novel concept, double-entry accounting. This invention revolutionized business practice and made Pacioli a celebrity. His was one of the first books to be printed on the Gutenberg press.弗拉·卢卡·帕乔利（Fra Luca de Pacioli，1445–1517 年）1494 年出版了他的奠基之作《算术、几何、比例和比例性知识大全》（The Collected Knowledge of Arithmetic, Geometry, Proportion, and Proportionality）。在书中一节，帕乔利描述了一个新颖的概念——复式记账。这项发明彻底改变了商业实践，也使帕乔利成了名人。他的著作是最早用古腾堡印刷机印制的书籍之一。 was a big virtue effect in economics. It made business more controllable, and it made it more honest.

我自幼便清楚，经济中有巨大的美德效应，也有巨大的恶行效应。但当你谈论美德与恶行379Virtue and vice美德与恶行时，经济学家会极不自在。这玩意儿不便于列成一大堆数字。但我认为经济中确有巨大的美德效应。我会说，修士卢卡·帕乔利380Fra Luca de PacioliFra Luca de Pacioli (1445–1517) in 1494 published his seminal work, The Collected Knowledge of Arithmetic, Geometry, Proportion, and Proportionality. In one section of the book, Pacioli described a novel concept, double-entry accounting. This invention revolutionized business practice and made Pacioli a celebrity. His was one of the first books to be printed on the Gutenberg press.弗拉·卢卡·帕乔利（Fra Luca de Pacioli，1445–1517 年）1494 年出版了他的奠基之作《算术、几何、比例和比例性知识大全》（The Collected Knowledge of Arithmetic, Geometry, Proportion, and Proportionality）。在书中一节，帕乔利描述了一个新颖的概念——复式记账。这项发明彻底改变了商业实践，也使帕乔利成了名人。他的著作是最早用古腾堡印刷机印制的书籍之一。（Fra Luca de Pacioli）推广复式簿记，便是经济中一个巨大的美德效应。它让商业更易掌控，也更诚实。

“当你谈论美德与恶行时，经济学家会极不自在。这玩意儿不便于列成一大堆数字。

“Economists get very uncomfortable when you talk about virtue and vice. It doesn’t lend itself to a lot of columns of numbers.”当你谈起德行与恶行，经济学家会极不自在。因为这东西不适于列成成排的数字。

Then the cash register.381cash register收银机 The cash register did more for human morality than the congregational church. It was a really powerful phenomenon to make an economic system work better, just as in reverse, a system that can be easily defrauded ruins a civilization. A system that’s very hard to defraud, like a cash register–based system, helps the economic performance of a civilization by reducing vice, but very few people within economics talk about it in those terms.

再说说收款机。收款机对人类道德的贡献，胜过公理教会（Congregational Church）。它确实是一种让经济系统运转得更好的强大现象，正如反过来说，一个易被欺诈钻空子的系统会毁掉文明。一个极难被欺诈的系统，比如以收款机为基础的系统，能通过减少恶行而提升文明的济绩效，但经济学界极少有人用这样的语言谈论它。

I’ll go further: I say economic systems work better when there’s an extreme reliability ethos. The traditional way to get a reliability ethos, at least in past generations in America, was through religion. The religions instilled guilt. We have a charming Irish Catholic priest in our neighborhood, and he loves to say, “Those old Jews may have invented guilt, but we perfected it.” This guilt, derived from religion, has been a huge driver of a reliability ethos, which has been very helpful to economic outcomes for man.

我还要进一步说：当存在极端的诚信精神时，经济系统运转得更好。至少在过往几代美国人中，养成诚信精神的传统途径是宗教。宗教灌输负罪感。我们邻里有一位迷人的爱尔兰天主教神父，他爱说：“那些老犹太人或许发明了负罪感，但我们把它完善了。”这种源自宗教的负罪感，是诚信精神的巨大驱动力量，对人类的经济成果助益良多。

Many bad effects from vice are clear. You’ve got the crazy booms and crooked promotions—all you have to do is read the paper over the last six months. There’s enough vice to make us all choke. And by the way, everybody’s angry about unfair compensation at the top of American corporations, and people should be. We now face various crazy governance nostrums invented by lawyers and professors that won’t give us a fix for unfair compensation, yet a good partial solution is obvious: If directors were significant shareholders who got a pay of zero, you’d be amazed what would happen to unfair compensation of corporate executives as we dampened effects from reciprocity tendency.

恶行造成的许多恶果显而易见。那些疯狂的泡沫与奸诈的促销——你只需翻翻过去半年的报纸。其中的恶行足以让我们全都窒息。顺带一提，人人都对公司高层的薪酬不公感到愤怒，他们也该愤怒。如今我们面对律师和教授们发明的各种疯狂治理妙方，却无助于解决薪酬不公；然而一个良好的部分解法是显而易见的：若董事都是薪酬为零的大股东，当我们削弱互惠倾向的影响时，你会发现公司高管的薪酬不公会发生何等惊人的变化。

A roughly similar equivalent of this no-pay system has been tried in a strange place. In England, lay magistrates382Lay magistrates非专业治安法官 staff the lower criminal courts, which can send you to prison for a year or fine you substantially. You’ve got three judges sitting up there, and they all get a pay of zero. Their expenses are reimbursed, but not too liberally. And they work about 40 half-days a year as volunteers. It’s worked beautifully for about 700 years. Able and honest people compete to become magistrates, to perform the duty and get the significance but no pay.

这种无薪酬制度的一个大致相似的版本，曾在一个奇怪的地方试行。在英国（England），由非专职的治安法官（lay magistrates）主持下级刑事法庭，他们可将你判入狱一年或课以重罚。三位法官高坐其上，薪酬皆为零。他们的开支可报销，但并不宽裕。他们每年作为志愿者工作约40个半天。这套制度漂亮地运转了约700年。能干而诚实的人竞相争当治安法官，履行职责、获得声望，却分文不取。

This is the system Benjamin Franklin, near the end of his life, wanted for the US government. He didn’t want the high executives of government to be paid but to be like himself or the entirely unpaid, well-off ministers and rulers of the Mormon Church. And when I see what’s happened in California, I’m not sure he wasn’t right. At any rate, no one now drifts in Franklin’s direction. For one thing, professors—and most of them need money—get appointed directors.

这便是本杰明·富兰克林324Benjamin Franklin本杰明·富兰克林（Benjamin Franklin）晚年希望美国政府采用的制度。他不欲政府高官领薪，而希望他们像他自己，或像摩门教会（Mormon Church）中那些完全无薪、家境宽裕的牧师与领袖。当我看到加州（California）的现状，我不敢说他错了。无论如何，如今已无人朝富兰克林的方向靠拢。原因之一在于，教授们——他们大多需要钱——被委任为董事。

It is not always recognized that to function best, morality should sometimes appear unfair, like most worldly outcomes. The craving for perfect fairness causes a lot of terrible problems in system function. Some systems should be made deliberately unfair to individuals because they’ll be fairer on average for all of us. Thus, there can be virtue in apparent non-fairness.

人们往往没有认识到：为求最佳运转，道德有时应显得不公，一如世间大多数结果。对完美公平的渴望，会给系统运转带来许多可怕的问题。某些制度应被刻意设计得对个体不公，因为对我们所有人平均而言，它们会更公平。因此，表面的不公之中亦可藏有美德。

“对完美公平的渴望，会给系统运转带来许多可怕的问题。

“The craving for perfect fairness causes a lot of terrible problems in system function.”对绝对公平的渴求，会给系统运作带来许多糟糕的问题。

I frequently cite the example of having your career over in the Navy if your ship goes aground,383Ship goes aground船只搁浅 even if it wasn’t your fault. I say the lack of justice for the one guy who wasn’t at fault is way more than made up by a greater justice for everybody when every captain of a ship always sweats blood to make sure the ship doesn’t go aground. Tolerating a little unfairness to some to get a greater fairness for all is a model I recommend to all of you. But again, I wouldn’t put it in your assigned college work if you want to be graded well, particularly in a modern law school wherein there is usually an overlove of fairness-seeking process.

我常举海军的例子：若你的船搁浅，383Ship goes aground船只搁浅哪怕并非你的过失，你的军旅生涯也就此终结。我说，当每位舰长都呕心沥血确保舰船不搁浅时，全体人获得的更大公正，远胜过对那一位无过者不公的补偿。容忍对部分人的些许不公，以换取对所有人更大的公平——这是我推荐给诸位的模式。但同样，若你想得好分数，我劝你别把它写进布置的作业，尤其在那些通常过度迷恋追求公平程序的现代法学院里。

There are, of course, enormous vice effects in economics. You have these bubbles with so much fraud and folly. The aftermath is frequently very unpleasant, and we’ve had some of that lately. One of the first big bubbles, of course, was the huge and horrible South Sea Bubble384The South Sea BubbleThe South Sea Bubble was an economic frenzy in England that occurred when speculation in South Sea Company shares peaked during 1720. The share price rose from \xa3128 in January to a high of \xa31,000 in August then fell back to \xa3150 in September. The company had been granted exclusive trading rights in Spanish South America. When results ultimately proved skimpy, the company engineered a public debt scheme that appeared to bolster profits. Company leaders and other shareholders also talked up future revenues, causing the speculative frenzy. Public outcry following disclosure of the fraud led to imposition of the Bubble Act of 1720, requiring publicly traded companies to have a royal charter.南海泡沫（The South Sea Bubble）是英国的一场经济狂热，发生在 1720 年对南海公司股票的投机达到顶峰之际。股价从 1 月的 128 英镑涨到 8 月 1,000 英镑的高点，9 月又回落到 150 英镑。该公司获得了在西班牙南美洲的独家贸易权。当最终业绩显得微薄时，公司设计了一个看似能提振利润的公共债务方案。公司领导层和其他股东也吹嘘未来营收，引发了投机狂热。骗局曝光后的公众义愤，促使英国出台了 1720 年的《泡沫法》（Bubble Act），要求公开上市公司必须持有皇家特许状。 in England. The aftermath was interesting.

当然，经济中亦有巨大的恶行效应。那些泡沫充斥着欺诈与愚行。泡沫破裂后的余波往往极不愉快，而我们近来便尝过一些。最早的大泡沫之一，自然是英国（England）那场巨大而可怕的南海泡沫384The South Sea BubbleThe South Sea Bubble was an economic frenzy in England that occurred when speculation in South Sea Company shares peaked during 1720. The share price rose from \xa3128 in January to a high of \xa31,000 in August then fell back to \xa3150 in September. The company had been granted exclusive trading rights in Spanish South America. When results ultimately proved skimpy, the company engineered a public debt scheme that appeared to bolster profits. Company leaders and other shareholders also talked up future revenues, causing the speculative frenzy. Public outcry following disclosure of the fraud led to imposition of the Bubble Act of 1720, requiring publicly traded companies to have a royal charter.南海泡沫（The South Sea Bubble）是英国的一场经济狂热，发生在 1720 年对南海公司股票的投机达到顶峰之际。股价从 1 月的 128 英镑涨到 8 月 1,000 英镑的高点，9 月又回落到 150 英镑。该公司获得了在西班牙南美洲的独家贸易权。当最终业绩显得微薄时，公司设计了一个看似能提振利润的公共债务方案。公司领导层和其他股东也吹嘘未来营收，引发了投机狂热。骗局曝光后的公众义愤，促使英国出台了 1720 年的《泡沫法》（Bubble Act），要求公开上市公司必须持有皇家特许状。（South Sea Bubble）。其后续颇有意味。

Many of you probably don’t remember what happened after the South Sea Bubble, which caused an enormous financial contraction and a lot of pain. Except in certain rare cases, they banned publicly traded stock in England for decades. Parliament passed a law that said you can have a partnership with a few partners but you can’t have publicly traded stock. And by the way, England continued to grow without publicly traded stock. The people who are in the business of prospering because there’s a lot of stock being traded in casino-like frenzy wouldn’t like this example if they studied it enough.

你们多半不记得南海泡沫之后发生了什么——它引发了剧烈的金融收缩与巨大痛苦。除少数特例外，英国（England）禁止公开发行股票长达数十年。议会立法规定：你可以与少数合伙人组建合伙制企业，但不得公开发行股票。顺带一提，没有公开发行股票，英国照样增长。那些靠炒股狂热般赌场式交易发财的人，若细究此例，定不会喜欢它。

It didn’t ruin England to have a long period when they didn’t have publicly traded shares. Just as in real estate—we had all the shopping centers and auto dealerships and so on we needed for years when we didn’t have publicly traded real estate shares. It’s a myth that once you’ve got some capital market, economic considerations demand that it has to be as fast and efficient as a casino. It doesn’t.

长期没有公开发行股票，并未毁掉英国。正如房地产——当没有公开发行的房地产股份时，我们多年来照样建起了所需的所有购物中心、汽车经销店等等。一旦有了资本市场，经济考量就要求它快如赌场、高效如赌场，这是个谬见。事实并非如此。

Another interesting problem is raised by vice effects involving envy. Envy wisely got a very strong condemnation in the laws of Moses.385Laws of Moses摩西律法 You remember how they laid it on with a trowel: You couldn’t covet thy neighbor’s ass, you couldn’t covet thy neighbor’s servant girl, you couldn’t covet… Those old Jews knew how envious people are and how much trouble it caused. They really laid it on hard, and they were right.

涉及妒忌的恶行效应，引出了另一个有趣的问题。妒忌在摩西（Moses）律法中受到了明智而严厉的谴责。你们记得他们是多么不遗余力地强调：不可贪恋邻舍的驴，不可贪恋邻舍的婢女，不可贪恋……那些老犹太人深知人性多妒，也深知这会惹出多大麻烦。他们确实施加得极重，而他们是对的。

But [Bernard de] Mandeville386Bernard de MandevilleBernard de Mandeville (1670–1733) , philosopher and satirist, published a poem, “The Fable of the Bees: or, Private Vices, Publick Benefits,” in 1705 as a political satire. Mandeville’s philosophy suggests that altruism harms the state and its intellectual progress, and that self-interested human vice is the real engine of progress. Thus, he arrives at the paradox that “private vices are public benefits.”伯纳德·德·曼德维尔（Bernard de Mandeville，1670–1733 年）是哲学家和讽刺作家，1705 年他出版了一首诗作为政治讽刺——《蜜蜂的寓言：或，私人之恶、公众之利》（“The Fable of the Bees: or, Private Vices, Publick Benefits”）。曼德维尔的哲学暗示，利他主义损害国家及其智力进步，而自利的人性之恶才是进步的真正引擎。由此，他得出了“私人之恶即公众之利”的悖论。—remember his fable of bees?387The Fable of the Bees蜜蜂的寓言 He demonstrated convincingly, to me, anyway, that envy was a great driver of proclivity to spend. And so, here’s this terrible vice, which is forbidden in the Ten Commandments, and here it’s driving all these favorable results in economics. There’s some paradox in economics that nobody’s going to get out.

“这被十诫禁止的可怕恶行，此刻却驱动着经济中种种有利的结果。

—
The Ten Commandments
“Here’s this terrible vice, which is forbidden in the Ten Commandments, and here it’s driving all these favorable results in economics.”这边是一种在《十诫》中被禁的可怕恶行，那边它却在经济学里驱动着种种有利的结果。

When I was young, everybody was excited by [Kurt] Gxf6del,389Kurt G\xf6delKurt G\xf6del (1906–1978) , a logician, mathematician, and philosopher of mathematics from Austria-Hungary, wrote a dissertation for his PhD at the University of Vienna that included his famous, but somewhat obscure, incompleteness theorems. The first theorem holds that one can use the mathematical system to construct a statement that can be neither proved nor disproved within that system. The second theorem, arrived at by proving the first, states that no consistent system can be used to prove its own consistency.库尔特·哥德尔（Kurt Gödel，1906–1978 年）是来自奥匈帝国的逻辑学家、数学家和数学哲学家，他在维也纳大学攻读博士的论文包含了他著名但颇为晦涩的不完备性定理。第一定理认为，人们可以用一个数学系统构造出一个在该系统内既不能被证明也不能被否证的命题。第二定理通过证明第一定理得出，它指出，任何一致的系统都不能被用来证明它自身的一致性。 who came up with proof that you couldn’t have a mathematical system without a lot of irritating incompleteness in it. Well, since then, my betters tell me that they’ve come up with more irremovable defects in mathematics and have decided that you’re never going to get mathematics without some paradox in it. No matter how hard you work, you’re going to have to live with some paradox if you’re a mathematician.

我年轻时，人人都为哥德尔389Kurt G\xf6delKurt G\xf6del (1906–1978) , a logician, mathematician, and philosopher of mathematics from Austria-Hungary, wrote a dissertation for his PhD at the University of Vienna that included his famous, but somewhat obscure, incompleteness theorems. The first theorem holds that one can use the mathematical system to construct a statement that can be neither proved nor disproved within that system. The second theorem, arrived at by proving the first, states that no consistent system can be used to prove its own consistency.库尔特·哥德尔（Kurt Gödel，1906–1978 年）是来自奥匈帝国的逻辑学家、数学家和数学哲学家，他在维也纳大学攻读博士的论文包含了他著名但颇为晦涩的不完备性定理。第一定理认为，人们可以用一个数学系统构造出一个在该系统内既不能被证明也不能被否证的命题。第二定理通过证明第一定理得出，它指出，任何一致的系统都不能被用来证明它自身的一致性。（Kurt Gödel）兴奋，他证明了任何数学系统都难免许多恼人的不完备。自那以后，比我高明的人告诉我，他们在数学中发现了更多无法消除的缺陷，并认定：没有悖论的数学是不存在的。无论你多努力，若你是数学家，就只得与某些悖论共存。

Well, if the mathematicians can’t get the paradox out of their system when they’re creating it themselves, the poor economists are never going to get rid of paradoxes, nor are any of the rest of us. It doesn’t matter. Life is interesting with some paradox. When I run into a paradox, I think either I’m a total horse’s ass to have gotten to this point or I’m fruitfully near the edge of my discipline. It adds excitement to life to wonder which it is.

好吧，连数学家在自己创造的体系中都无法剔除悖论，可怜的经济学家永远摆脱不了悖论，我们其他人也一样。那也无妨。生活有点悖论才有趣。每遇悖论，我便想：要么我是个彻头彻尾的蠢材，才走到这一步；要么我正富有成效地逼近本学科的边界。琢磨究竟属于哪一种，给生活平添了刺激。

“生活有点悖论才有趣。

“Life is interesting with some paradox.”生活因几分悖论而有趣。

As I conclude, I want to tell one more story demonstrating how awful it is to get a wrong idea from a limited repertoire and just stick to it. This is the story of Hyman Liebowitz, who came to America from the old country. In the new country, as in the old, he tried to make his way in the family trade, which was manufacturing nails. And he struggled, and he struggled, and finally his little nail business got to vast prosperity, and his wife said to him, “You are old, Hyman. It’s time to go to Florida and turn the business over to our son.”

收尾之际，我想再讲一个故事，说明从有限的知识库存里得出错误观念便执迷不悟，是何等可怕。这是海曼·利伯维茨（Hyman Liebowitz）的故事，他从旧大陆来到美国。在新国度，一如旧地，他尝试以家族手艺——制造铁钉——谋生。他奋斗，再奋斗，小小的铁钉生意终至极其兴旺；妻子对他说：“海曼，你老了，该去佛罗里达（Florida），把生意交给儿子了。”

So down he went to Florida, turning his business over to the son, but he got weekly financial reports. And he hadn’t been in Florida very long before they turned sharply negative. In fact, they were terrible. So he got on an airplane, and he went back to New Jersey where the factory was. As he left the airport on the way to the factory, he saw this enormous outdoor advertising sign lighted up. There was Jesus, spread out on the cross. And under it was a big legend: “They Used Liebowitz’s Nails.”

于是他南下佛罗里达，把生意交予儿子，却仍收到每周财务报表。他在佛州没住多久，报表便急转直下，实则糟糕透顶。于是他登机返回工厂所在地新泽西州（New Jersey）。离开机场前往工厂途中，他看到一块巨大的户外灯箱广告牌亮着：耶稣被钉在十字架上，下方一行大字：“他们用了利伯维茨的铁钉。”

So he stormed into the factory and said, “You dumb son! What do you think you’re doing? It took me 50 years to create this business!” “Papa,” the son said, “trust me. I will fix it.”

他怒气冲冲闯进工厂，喝道：“你这蠢儿子！你到底在干什么？我花了50年才创出这份家业！”“爸爸，”儿子说，“相信我。我会解决的。”

So back he went to Florida, and while he was in Florida, he got more reports, and the results kept getting worse. So he got on the airplane again. Left the airport, drove by the sign, looked up at this big lighted sign, and now there’s a vacant cross. And lo and behold, Jesus is crumpled on the ground under the cross, and the sign said, “They Didn’t Use Liebowitz’s Nails.”

于是他回到佛罗里达；在佛州期间，他又收到更多报表，业绩持续恶化。于是他再次登机。离开机场，驱车路过广告牌，抬头望那巨大的灯箱——如今十字架空了。看哪，耶稣蜷缩在十字架下的地上，广告语写着：“他们没有用利伯维茨的铁钉。”

Well, you can laugh at that. It is ridiculous, but it’s no more ridiculous than the way a lot of people cling to failed ideas.

嗯，你们尽可以笑。这很荒唐，但它并不比许多人死抱失败观念的样子更荒唐。

Keynes said, “It’s not bringing in the new ideas that’s so hard. It’s getting rid of the old ones.” And Einstein said it better, attributing his mental success to “curiosity, concentration, perseverance, and self-criticism.” By self-criticism, he meant becoming good at destroying your own best-loved and hardest-won ideas. If you can get really good at destroying your own wrong ideas, that is a great gift.

凯恩斯（John Maynard Keynes）说：“难的不在引入新观念，难在抛弃旧观念。”爱因斯坦（Albert Einstein）说得更好，他将自己思想上的成功归因于“好奇、专注、毅力与自省”。他所谓自省，是指善于摧毁自己最珍爱、最来之不易的观念。若你真能善于摧毁自己的错误观念，那便是一份大礼。

Well, it’s time to repeat the big lesson in this little talk. What I’ve urged is the use of a bigger multidisciplinary bag of tricks, mastered to fluency, to help economics and everything else. And I also urged that people not be discouraged by irremovable complexity and paradox. It just adds more fun to the problems. My inspiration again is Keynes: Better roughly right than precisely wrong.

好，是时候复述这场小演讲的大教训了。我所力倡的，是使用一套更大、更融会贯通的多学科诀窍，以助经济学及其他一切。我也力倡人们莫因无法消除的复杂与悖论而气馁。那只会给问题增添更多乐趣。我的灵感仍来自凯恩斯：粗略的正确，胜过精准的错误。

And so, I end by repeating what I said once before on a similar occasion. If you skillfully follow the multidisciplinary path, you will never wish to come back. It would be like cutting off your hands.

于是，我以重复昔日相似场合说过的话作结：若你巧妙地踏上跨学科之路，你将永不愿回头。那就像砍掉自己的双手。

Well, that’s the end. I’ll take questions as long as people can endure me.

好，到此结束。只要大家还能忍受我，我就一直回答提问。

Audience member: [The question was garbled, but the person asked about derivatives, which Buffett has called “financial weapons of mass destruction.”] Buffett said that the genie’s out of the bottle and the hangover may be proportionate to the binge. Would you speculate for us how that scenario can play out?

听众：［问题有些含混，但提问者问的是衍生品——巴菲特称之为“大规模金融杀伤性武器”。］巴菲特说过，精灵已经跳出了瓶子，而宿醉的量或许与狂欢的量相当。您能否为我们推测一下，那种局面会如何上演？

Well, of course, catastrophe predictions have always been quite difficult to make with success. But I confidently predict that there are big troubles to come. The system is almost insanely irresponsible. And what people think are fixes aren’t really fixes. It’s so complicated I can’t do it justice here, but you can’t believe the trillions of dollars involved. You can’t believe the complexity. You can’t believe how difficult it is to do the accounting. You can’t believe how big the incentives are to have wishful thinking about values and wishful thinking about ability to clear.

当然，成功预言灾难向来极难。但我自信地预言：大麻烦将至。这个体系简直疯狂地不负责任。人们以为的修补，并非真正的修补。它太复杂，我在此无法尽述——但你们无法相信涉及的金额高达数万亿美元，无法相信其复杂程度，无法相信做账有多难，也无法相信激励机制会让人对价值、对清算能力产生多大的如意算盘。

Running off a derivative book is agony and takes time. You saw what happened when they tried to run off the derivative books at Enron. Its certified net worth vanished. In the derivative books of America, there are a lot of reported profits that were never earned and assets that never existed.

清掉一本衍生品账册是痛苦的，且极费时。你们看到了安然公司（Enron）试图清算衍生品账册时发生了什么——其核定的净资产凭空消失。在美国的衍生品账册上，有许多从未赚得的报称利润，以及从未存在的资产。

fig 390
—
Lewis Carroll and the Mad Hatter’s tea party刘易斯·卡罗尔与疯帽匠的茶会

There are large febezzlement effects and some ordinary embezzlement effects that come from derivative activity. And the reversal of these is going to cause pain. How big the pain will be and how well it will be handled, I can’t tell you. But you would be disgusted if you had a fair mind and spent a month really delving into a big derivative operation. You would think it was Lewis Carroll. You would think it was the Mad Hatter’s tea party. And the false precision of these people is just unbelievable. They make the worst economics professors look like gods. Moreover, there is depravity augmenting the folly.

衍生品活动带来了巨大的“捞灰金”效应，以及一些普通的贪污效应。而这些效应的逆转将引发痛苦。痛苦有多大、将如何处理，我无从奉告。但若你心存公正，花一个月认真钻研一家大型衍生品业务，定会作呕。你会觉得那是刘易斯·卡洛尔（Lewis Carroll）的荒诞世界，是疯帽匠的茶话会（Mad Hatter’s Tea Party）。而此辈虚假的精确简直令人难以置信。他们让最差劲的经济学教授看起来都像神祇。更有甚者，在愚行之外还有败德相佐。

Read the book Fiasco, by law professor and former derivatives trader Frank Partnoy, an insider account of depravity in derivative trading at one of the biggest and best-regarded Wall Street firms. The book will turn your stomach.

去读《诚信的背后》（Fiasco）一书吧，作者弗兰克·帕特诺伊（Frank Partnoy）是法学教授、前衍生品交易员，书中以内幕视角揭露华尔街上最受推崇的巨头之一在衍生品交易中的败德之行。这本书会让你反胃。

Could you describe Warren’s reaction to the negative reaction he got from musing about the defects of California’s Prop 13?Was he shocked, surprised?

您能否描述一下，沃伦对人们就他揣测加州第 13 号提案（Prop 13）缺陷所流露的负面反应作何反应？他是震惊，还是意外？

Prop 13?

第 13 号提案？

It’s hard to shock Warren. He’s past 70; he’s seen a lot. And his brain works quickly. He generally avoids certain subjects before elections, and that is what I am going to do here.

要让沃伦（Warren Buffett）震惊可不容易。他年逾七十，见多识广，头脑反应极快。选举前他通常回避某些话题，而在此我也打算如此。
